sentences.en: Instead of having Tcl scripts interact directly with the C-based control plane, Cisco now encourages running Python 3 inside a Guest Shell container, as it doesn't treat strings as hardware-level logic by default and instead interacts with the router via structured APIs (like cli.execute() or NETCONF/YANG models) rather than raw string evaluation.
sentences.zh: 思科现在鼓励在 Guest Shell 容器内运行 Python 3，而不是让 Tcl 脚本直接与基于 C 的控制平面交互，因为默认情况下它不会将字符串视为硬件级逻辑，而是通过结构化 API（如 cli.execute() 或 NETCONF/YANG 模型）而不是原始字符串评估与路由器交互。

blocks.html_en: Tcl's homoiconicity was a design shortcut that made Tcl easy to embed in the 90s but makes it less favorable today, when more and more focus is on security, even if it comes at a price of more rigid rules and structures. The world of modern networking is just way too vast and wild to ignore the risks that widespread use of a homoiconic language would carry. Modern CPUs and static analyzers are now far more capable of optimizing and securing rigidly structured languages. These tools reduce the cognitive load on developers by detecting errors and vulnerabilities much earlier in the development cycle. It's a safety net that a language as fluid as Tcl simply can't provide.

blocks.html_en: Guess what — you don't have to treat data as code, unless you choose to! You can develop tools and GUIs with just the "default" set of Tcl/Tk commands and extensions. But the door is always open. In C#, JavaScript, Python and the like, such power belongs to the compiler team at Microsoft, Mozilla or the Python Software Foundation. In Tcl, the power belongs to whoever is writing a script.

But over time, you'll understand it better, and might even use it to your benefit. For example — to create whole sets of custom commands, operators and program flows in the form of Domain Specific Languages (DSLs).

blocks.html_en: As you get more experienced with Tcl, you'll gradually transition into a "Tcl way" of thinking, and naturally steer more towards the initial purpose of this tool command language: from tool development, scripting and automation, to "gluing" application components together. Here Tcl/Tk truly shines, providing a portable, native-looking interface to help manage high-performance, natively compiled binaries doing the heavy lifting. We’ll explore how to bridge these two worlds later in this article.

blocks.html_en: Although not very "popular", Tcl/Tk is still actively developed by the Tcl/Tk Core Development Team. On Nov 13, 2025, 12 years after the release Tcl 8.6, they presented a new major version of Tcl — Tcl/Tk 9.0.

blocks.html_en: It's a truly milestone release, as it made Tcl a fully 64-bit-aware language. It might seem puzzling and even silly why this wasn't done sooner, but you can already guess what such a transition brings: it changes the pointer size from 32 to 64 bit. Meaning, some of the existing Tcl scripts, especially those embedding pure C code (critcl package) could either stop working or exhibit unexpected behavior. And since Tcl historically provided outstanding backwards-compatibility, the core team of devs had to be very careful while implementing and introducing such an update, while maintaining compatibility with as much of the existing, sometimes decades-old code-base, as possible. This takes time.

blocks.html_en: • Tcl now natively supports the ZipFS virtual filesystem. After years of having to rely on 3rd-party hacks and products to create self-sufficient apps or bundle data with scripts, you can now attach a zip file to a script and mount it as a virtual access point to access the files and the directories inside. We'll talk more about this important feature in the Tcl 9 And ZipFS section

blocks.html_en: • Octal Literal Sanitization by default — in Tcl 8.x, 010 was interpreted as octal (8), which led to endless "WTF is with this math?!" bugs when handling leading zeros, like zip codes or dates. blocks.html_en: • Overall more strict treatment of data. Tcl 8.x could sometimes try and "be smart" when reading text files by silently substituting invalid byte sequences with replacement characters or falling back to ISO-8859-1 (Latin-1) when it encountered encoding errors. While this prevented scripts from crashing, it often led to unexpected data corruption that was nearly impossible to debug once the data was saved. In Tcl 9.0, this behavior has been replaced by a formal Encoding Profile system. So while in Tcl 8.x, if you read a file as UTF-8 that contained a stray non-UTF-8 byte, Tcl would often just carry on, Tcl 9.0's default profile is now strict. If Tcl encounters an invalid byte sequence for the specified encoding, it will immediately throw an error, which is paramount for cross-platform tool development. I know this, because for the past year I had to deal with lots of arbitrarily-encoded files, and am grateful that Tcl let me know right away when something was wrong with a file I was working with. A file that C# and Python deemed perfectly fine BTW, as "being smart" is a feature of both. Tl;dr: Tcl 8.x assumed the programmer wanted the program to keep running at all costs. Tcl 9.0 assumes the programmer wants the data to be correct at all costs.

sentences.en: As interesting a topic as Tcl is, there's one feature of the Tcl/Tk toolkit that's so ubiquitous and versatile, that people often forget that it has any relation to Tcl at all:

blocks.html_en: Let's not beat around the bush and get to the key reason why Tcl is especially relevant today, just as it's been for the past decades — the Tk GUI Toolkit. Soon after the first public release of Tcl, John Ousterhout realized that the world of compute was rapidly moving towards more user-friendly graphical user interfaces. He also knew that there existed several competing operating systems, each — with its own implementation of the UI APIs. This led to the creation of Tk, which became an essential part of Tcl as we know it. So essential, that the "general identity name" of the language itself was changed to Tcl/Tk as a result.

sentences.en: Let's not beat around the bush and get to the key reason why Tcl is especially relevant today, just as it's been for the past decades — the Tk GUI Toolkit.
sentences.zh: 让我们不拐弯抹角，直接了解 Tcl 在今天特别重要的关键原因（就像过去几十年一样）——Tk GUI 工具包。

blocks.html_en: Over time, Mr. Ousterhout chose to turn Tk into a cross-platform toolkit, making sure the same Tcl code could be used (with minimal changes) to create GUIs on different platforms.

blocks.html_en: Tk is the original "Write Once, Run Anywhere" UI. Long before Electron was consuming all the RAM in the world, Tk was providing a lightweight bridge between Windows, macOS, and X11 with a footprint that makes an empty C# binary look bloated. Due to this fact, Tk has been so widespread in professional circles (automotive, chip industry, astronomy) that any attempt to estimate how many interfaces were implemented in Tk, as well as are still used, is completely futile.

sentences.en: Long before Electron was consuming all the RAM in the world, Tk was providing a lightweight bridge between Windows, macOS, and X11 with a footprint that makes an empty C# binary look bloated.

blocks.html_en: In fact, Tk became so powerful and portable, that languages like Python, Perl, and Ruby actually adopted it as their standard library, like Python's tkinter we'll look at later.

blocks.html_en: However, if you only look at the screenshots of the decades-old Tk interfaces, you might get an impression that Tk GUI is ugly. Indeed, for 20 years since its inception, Tk didn't come with ttk — Themed set of Tk widgets. It looked like Windows 3.11 or 95 UI on every platform: gray, boxy, with very spartan decoration options. So over time most developers moved to the web or Qt before Tk finally got native-looking. They haven't looked back to see that it’s fixed.

blocks.html_en: Being cross-platform, Tk UI kit doesn't expose native Win32 DLL calls or Linux X11/macOS Cocoa inner workings, and therefore any interaction that needs to happen needs to be programmed in explicitly. Thankfully, Tk provides high-level abstractions, also known as "widgets", which do most of the heavy-lifting, while exposing the necessary controls for the programmers. The way these widgets fall into the Tcl architecture is also extremely elegant — each Tk widget exists as a command! They aren't static elements, but in a way "objects" with their own "methods" which they provide to be configured.

In other words, the scrollbar takes that .mclist.tree yview command and appends arguments to it, like so: lappend command "moveto" 0.5, ending up with the complete command string {.mclist.tree yview "moveto" 0.5}, which it then executes (in a way similar to the eval $command) instructing the treeview to shift its internal coordinate system to a new position

blocks.html_en: See how Tcl hides nothing from you? It literally builds up command strings, and executes them as instructed. This means that you can both replicate "native" window controls, as well as make any elements control any number of other elements, while building a portable, cross-platform GUI. Most modern frameworks like Electron, Flutter or SwiftUI hide this "handshaking" logic behind Reactive State or Data Binding, acting like "black boxes", stifling growth of developers and leading to all sorts of hard to find bugs and performance issues. Not to say that you won't have bugs in your Tcl scripts, but in the vast majority of cases those will be entirely your fault, easy to diagnose and fix. Very refreshing!

blocks.html_en: Also, note how the -command callbacks are passed as lists in the example. This is considered good practice when building up callbacks for Tk widgets or Tcl commands like eval, after, bind, subst, because [list …] items are "atomic". In Tcl, this prevents word-splitting bugs if callback arguments ever happen to contain spaces or special characters. In languages like JS, you pass a function reference with arguments: setTimeout(myFunc, 1000). In Tcl, you pass a string that the interpreter will parse and execute at a later time. You need to ensure that that at the time of the call, that string would contain a valid command string, where the command and all its arguments are properly grouped. A list will automatically enclose contents with whitespaces into {} braces, maintaining the required order and the number of items. It's one of those "Tcl'isms" you'll get used to as the time passes, and is the aforementioned "side-effect" of the "Everything is a String" principle, and the overall Tcl's syntax, where commands and arguments are separated by whitespace.

blocks.html_en: As for the widget interaction, such rigid coupling works well for closely-related elements (like a scrollbar in a window, or an array of checkboxes on a canvas). However, to set up communication between systems you should look for another approach. Building UIs with separate windows and contexts with tight couplings via -command parameters is OK for small tools or while learning Tk. As soon as your program grows beyond 2-3 windows, you'll notice how managing those dependencies becomes more difficult.

sentences.en: As for the widget interaction, such rigid coupling works well for closely-related elements (like a scrollbar in a window, or an array of checkboxes on a canvas).
sentences.zh: 至于小部件交互，这种刚性耦合对于密切相关的元素（例如窗口中的滚动条或画布上的复选框数组）非常有效。

sentences.en: However, to set up communication between systems you should look for another approach.
sentences.zh: 但是，要在系统之间建立通信，您应该寻找另一种方法。

sentences.en: Building UIs with separate windows and contexts with tight couplings via -command parameters is OK for small tools or while learning Tk.
sentences.zh: 对于小工具或学习 Tk 时，通过 -command 参数构建具有独立窗口和上下文的 UI 并具有紧密耦合是可以的。

sentences.en: As soon as your program grows beyond 2-3 windows, you'll notice how managing those dependencies becomes more difficult.
sentences.zh: 一旦您的程序增长超过 2-3 个窗口，您就会注意到管理这些依赖关系变得更加困难。

blocks.html_en: Thankfully, there's an elegant and robust solution.

sentences.en: Thankfully, there's an elegant and robust solution.
sentences.zh: 值得庆幸的是，有一个优雅而强大的解决方案。

blocks.html_en: Tcl/Tk — Data-Oriented and Event-Driven by Design

sentences.en: Tcl/Tk — Data-Oriented and Event-Driven by Design
sentences.zh: Tcl/Tk — 面向数据和事件驱动的设计

blocks.html_en: Here's where Tcl/Tk really shines, and why I chose to spend almost half a year writing this article to demonstrate how the toolkit could become a "manager's best friend" as a powerful, cross-platform programmatic "glue" to robustly tie together systems and components.

sentences.en: Here's where Tcl/Tk really shines, and why I chose to spend almost half a year writing this article to demonstrate how the toolkit could become a "manager's best friend" as a powerful, cross-platform programmatic "glue" to robustly tie together systems and components.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Tcl/Tk 真正闪光的地方，也是为什么我选择花近半年的时间来写这篇文章来演示该工具包如何成为“经理最好的朋友”，作为强大的跨平台编程“粘合剂”，将系统和组件牢固地结合在一起。

blocks.html_en: In the code block above I mentioned some "event loop". It's a special control mechanism that manages the processing of tasks and external inputs in a non-blocking, single-threaded environment.

sentences.en: In the code block above I mentioned some "event loop".
sentences.zh: 在上面的代码块中我提到了一些“事件循环”。

sentences.en: It's a special control mechanism that manages the processing of tasks and external inputs in a non-blocking, single-threaded environment.
sentences.zh: 它是一种特殊的控制机制，用于在非阻塞、单线程环境中管理任务和外部输入的处理。

blocks.html_en: Simply speaking, Tcl's event loop continuously processes events, pulled from the event queue, usually dozens of times a second. It watches for mouse or keyboard events, invoking command callbacks and event bindings as needed. Most importantly, event loop works with queues — either you, or some commands in your code, or the OS itself can queue certain actions as events or callbacks, which the event queue then processes in an orderly manner.

sentences.en: Simply speaking, Tcl's event loop continuously processes events, pulled from the event queue, usually dozens of times a second.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，Tcl的事件循环不断地处理从事件队列中拉出的事件，通常每秒处理几十次。

sentences.en: It watches for mouse or keyboard events, invoking command callbacks and event bindings as needed.
sentences.zh: 它监视鼠标或键盘事件，根据需要调用命令回调和事件绑定。

sentences.en: Most importantly, event loop works with queues — either you, or some commands in your code, or the OS itself can queue certain actions as events or callbacks, which the event queue then processes in an orderly manner.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，事件循环与队列一起工作——无论是您，还是代码中的某些命令，或者操作系统本身都可以将某些操作作为事件或回调进行排队，然后事件队列以有序的方式进行处理。

blocks.html_en: To understand the specifics of Tcl's event loop implementation refer to TkDocs, as they provide a well illustrated explanation.

sentences.en: To understand the specifics of Tcl's event loop implementation refer to TkDocs, as they provide a well illustrated explanation.
sentences.zh: 要了解 Tcl 事件循环实现的细节，请参阅 TkDocs，因为它们提供了详细的说明。

blocks.html_en: Event loop is a part of "pure Tcl", it's not something applicable only to Tk, but Tk cannot exist without the event loop. That's why each time you load in the Tk package, the event loop is started in the background for you.

sentences.en: Event loop is a part of "pure Tcl", it's not something applicable only to Tk, but Tk cannot exist without the event loop.
sentences.zh: 事件循环是“纯Tcl”的一部分，它不仅仅适用于Tk，但是如果没有事件循环，Tk就无法存在。

sentences.en: That's why each time you load in the Tk package, the event loop is started in the background for you.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么每次加载 Tk 包时，事件循环都会在后台为您启动。

blocks.html_en: For developers this means that with Tcl/Tk you can both react to system events (key presses, window size changes, mouse clicks and hovers etc.), as well as generate custom "virtual events" with data! Think of it as sending an envelope with a message to subscribers of a certain event. The contents of that envelope? — You get to both define and interpret as you please.

sentences.en: For developers this means that with Tcl/Tk you can both react to system events (key presses, window size changes, mouse clicks and hovers etc.), as well as generate custom "virtual events" with data!
sentences.zh: 对于开发人员来说，这意味着使用 Tcl/Tk 您既可以对系统事件（按键、窗口大小更改、鼠标单击和悬停等）做出反应，也可以使用数据生成自定义“虚拟事件”！

sentences.en: Think of it as sending an envelope with a message to subscribers of a certain event.
sentences.zh: 可以将其视为向特定事件的订阅者发送包含消息的信封。

sentences.en: The contents of that envelope? — You get to both define and interpret as you please.
sentences.zh: 那个信封里装的是什么？ — 您可以随心所欲地定义和解释。

sentences.zh: 在订阅者方面，无论它是 TclOO“对象”（使用 Tcl 9 回调）还是简单的过程：

blocks.html_en: This way your widget(s) can subscribe to a virtual event <<UI:Request:Submit>>, which your Event Manager would then publish with or without a "payload" attached.

sentences.en: This way your widget(s) can subscribe to a virtual event <<UI:Request:Submit>>, which your Event Manager would then publish with or without a "payload" attached.
sentences.zh: 这样，您的小部件就可以订阅虚拟事件 <<UI:Request:Submit>>，然后您的事件管理器将在附加或不附加“有效负载”的情况下发布该事件。

blocks.html_en: Think of this like C# Events and Delegates, or CustomEvent dispatch in JavaScript, or PyPubSub and blinker signals in Python.

sentences.en: Think of this like C# Events and Delegates, or CustomEvent dispatch in JavaScript, or PyPubSub and blinker signals in Python.
sentences.zh: 可以将其想象为 C# 事件和委托，或 JavaScript 中的 CustomEvent 调度，或 Python 中的 PyPubSub 和信号灯信号。

blocks.html_en: By emitting your own <<Virtual>> events and subscribing (or "binding") UI items and logic to those, you can build very complex GUIs without having to deal with hard coupling, whilst having all view elements independently react to anything happening to data in your program.

sentences.en: By emitting your own <<Virtual>> events and subscribing (or "binding") UI items and logic to those, you can build very complex GUIs without having to deal with hard coupling, whilst having all view elements independently react to anything happening to data in your program.
sentences.zh: 通过发出您自己的 <<Virtual>> 事件并订阅（或“绑定”）UI 项目和逻辑，您可以构建非常复杂的 GUI，而无需处理硬耦合，同时让所有视图元素独立地对程序中数据发生的任何情况做出反应。

Here it contains just 1 key-value pair {isValid 1}, but as you've seen, it can hold many more types of validation booleans or even free-form text messages depending on your goals. Here virtual events are used to set up communication between different widgets and windows, allowing any number of them to listen to events: popup windows, validators, the inspector window, the "Send" button. sentences.en: In the following demonstration the ValidationResult event's payload is sent to subscribers as a dict.
sentences.zh: 在下面的演示中，ValidationResult 事件的有效负载作为字典发送给订阅者。

sentences.en: Here it contains just 1 key-value pair {isValid 1}, but as you've seen, it can hold many more types of validation booleans or even free-form text messages depending on your goals.
sentences.zh: 这里它只包含 1 个键值对 {isValid 1}，但正如您所看到的，它可以容纳更多类型的验证布尔值，甚至可以根据您的目标容纳自由格式的文本消息。

sentences.en: Here virtual events are used to set up communication between different widgets and windows, allowing any number of them to listen to events: popup windows, validators, the inspector window, the "Send" button.
sentences.zh: 这里虚拟事件用于在不同的小部件和窗口之间建立通信，允许任意数量的小部件和窗口监听事件：弹出窗口、验证器、检查器窗口、“发送”按钮。

sentences.en: Or emit them with key presses and button clicks:
sentences.zh: 或者通过按键和点击按钮来发出它们：

blocks.html_en: Virtual events are a part of the Tk package and hence unavailable in "pure Tcl", because they need to bind to specific widgets. But this doesn't mean you can't extend your your EventManager class to make it go through a dict of subscribers and call the provided callbacks as commands, and not as Tk's virtual events.

sentences.en: Virtual events are a part of the Tk package and hence unavailable in "pure Tcl", because they need to bind to specific widgets.
sentences.zh: 虚拟事件是 Tk 包的一部分，因此在“纯 Tcl”中不可用，因为它们需要绑定到特定的小部件。

sentences.en: But this doesn't mean you can't extend your your EventManager class to make it go through a dict of subscribers and call the provided callbacks as commands, and not as Tk's virtual events.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着您不能扩展您的 EventManager 类以使其遍历订阅者字典并将提供的回调作为命令调用，而不是作为 Tk 的虚拟事件。

blocks.html_en: With such an event management class, you can do some cool things. How about a CLI tool with a pseudo-graphical interface driven by a "game loop"? Here a tick event is triggered every 50ms, and the appropriate commands are subscribed to it to draw their animated graphics into the console independently. The tick_count variable acts as a global timebase, allowing subscribers to calculate their animation phase by comparing the current tick to their internal "start" tick. Screen transitions are driven by an event that captures and broadcasts the input string.

sentences.en: With such an event management class, you can do some cool things.
sentences.zh: 通过这样的事件管理类，您可以做一些很酷的事情。

sentences.en: How about a CLI tool with a pseudo-graphical interface driven by a "game loop"?
sentences.zh: 具有由“游戏循环”驱动的伪图形界面的 CLI 工具怎么样？

sentences.en: Here a tick event is triggered every 50ms, and the appropriate commands are subscribed to it to draw their animated graphics into the console independently.
sentences.zh: 这里每 50 毫秒触发一次刻度事件，并订阅相应的命令以将其动画图形独立绘制到控制台中。

sentences.en: The tick_count variable acts as a global timebase, allowing subscribers to calculate their animation phase by comparing the current tick to their internal "start" tick.
sentences.zh: tick_count 变量充当全局时基，允许订阅者通过将当前刻度与其内部“开始”刻度进行比较来计算其动画阶段。

sentences.en: Screen transitions are driven by an event that captures and broadcasts the input string.
sentences.zh: 屏幕转换由捕获和广播输入字符串的事件驱动。

blocks.html_en: All of this non-blocking goodness is running in a single thread. And we haven't even covered Tcl's threading capabilities yet! How many smoothly animated and responsive console apps have you seen as of late? Tcl excels in this regard due to its "event-first" philosophy.

sentences.en: All of this non-blocking goodness is running in a single thread.
sentences.zh: 所有这些非阻塞优点都在单个线程中运行。

sentences.en: And we haven't even covered Tcl's threading capabilities yet!
sentences.zh: 我们甚至还没有讨论 Tcl 的线程功能！

sentences.en: How many smoothly animated and responsive console apps have you seen as of late?
sentences.zh: 您最近见过多少个动画流畅、反应灵敏的控制台应用程序？

sentences.en: Tcl excels in this regard due to its "event-first" philosophy.
sentences.zh: Tcl在这方面的出色表现得益于其“事件至上”的理念。

blocks.html_en: By making systems communicate via events, you can create types of components, which would be very difficult to do with an imperative, tightly-coupled approach.

sentences.en: By making systems communicate via events, you can create types of components, which would be very difficult to do with an imperative, tightly-coupled approach.
sentences.zh: 通过使系统通过事件进行通信，您可以创建组件类型，而使用命令式、紧密耦合的方法很难做到这一点。

blocks.html_en: In the following example, the scrollbar widget is wired to act as a driver, or a "slider". It doesn't care who listens, and simply broadcasts how far its handle has traveled. Canvases have no clue that the scrollbar exists at all, and are simply listening a certain event, expecting a data "payload" with a 0-1 fraction multiplier. They take that value and independently calculate how far each one needs to travel. We could create ten windows with ten more canvases of different height, and they would auto-subscribe to a shared event and scroll together, or await some "private" events.

sentences.en: In the following example, the scrollbar widget is wired to act as a driver, or a "slider".
sentences.zh: 在下面的示例中，滚动条小部件被连接为充当驱动程序或“滑块”。

sentences.en: It doesn't care who listens, and simply broadcasts how far its handle has traveled.
sentences.zh: 它并不关心谁在听，而只是广播它的手柄已经移动了多远。

sentences.en: Canvases have no clue that the scrollbar exists at all, and are simply listening a certain event, expecting a data "payload" with a 0-1 fraction multiplier.
sentences.zh: 画布根本不知道滚动条是否存在，并且只是监听某个事件，期望具有 0-1 分数乘数的数据“有效负载”。

sentences.en: They take that value and independently calculate how far each one needs to travel.
sentences.zh: 他们获取该值并独立计算每个人需要行驶多远。

sentences.en: We could create ten windows with ten more canvases of different height, and they would auto-subscribe to a shared event and scroll together, or await some "private" events.
sentences.zh: 我们可以创建十个窗口，其中有十个不同高度的画布，它们会自动订阅共享事件并一起滚动，或者等待一些“私人”事件。

blocks.html_en: At any point we can destroy any of these UI components, and the program will continue to run without exceptions or "missing references", because there are none. There are only subscribers and events.

sentences.en: At any point we can destroy any of these UI components, and the program will continue to run without exceptions or "missing references", because there are none.
sentences.zh: 在任何时候，我们都可以销毁任何这些 UI 组件，并且程序将继续运行，不会出现异常或“丢失引用”，因为没有任何异常。

sentences.en: There are only subscribers and events.
sentences.zh: 只有订阅者和事件。

blocks.html_en: Such data-oriented, event-driven design lands itself perfectly into areas where high-performance, reliable, decoupled, and robust dual-sided synchronization of state is required. Particularly when building systems with clearly defined MVC-like roles. For instance, this is precisely why the Unity game engine team is so hell-bent on promoting their Data-Oriented Technology Stack, for it's the only type of architecture that can realistically be scaled almost infinitely, while allowing developers to transparently manage large systems.

sentences.en: Such data-oriented, event-driven design lands itself perfectly into areas where high-performance, reliable, decoupled, and robust dual-sided synchronization of state is required.
sentences.zh: 这种面向数据、事件驱动的设计非常适合需要高性能、可靠、解耦和强大的双面状态同步的领域。

sentences.en: Particularly when building systems with clearly defined MVC-like roles.
sentences.zh: 特别是在构建具有明确定义的类似 MVC 角色的系统时。

sentences.en: For instance, this is precisely why the Unity game engine team is so hell-bent on promoting their Data-Oriented Technology Stack, for it's the only type of architecture that can realistically be scaled almost infinitely, while allowing developers to transparently manage large systems.
sentences.zh: 例如，这正是 Unity 游戏引擎团队如此热衷于推广其面向数据的技术堆栈的原因，因为它是唯一一种可以实际上几乎无限扩展的架构类型，同时允许开发人员透明地管理大型系统。

blocks.html_en: Tcl/Tk is a perfect fit for this since its very first release!

sentences.en: Tcl/Tk is a perfect fit for this since its very first release!
sentences.zh: Tcl/Tk 自其第一个版本以来就非常适合此目的！

blocks.html_en: This approach is super effective and intuitive simply because Nature itself has already fundamentally "solved" systems communication, and the event-driven architecture is very close to how the real world "works". Like when humans and animals react to events and create new events, based on the information they receive and the skills, knowledge, resources and goals they have.

sentences.en: This approach is super effective and intuitive simply because Nature itself has already fundamentally "solved" systems communication, and the event-driven architecture is very close to how the real world "works".
sentences.zh: 这种方法非常有效和直观，因为大自然本身已经从根本上“解决”了系统通信，并且事件驱动的架构非常接近现实世界的“工作方式”。

sentences.en: Like when humans and animals react to events and create new events, based on the information they receive and the skills, knowledge, resources and goals they have.
sentences.zh: 就像人类和动物根据他们收到的信息以及他们拥有的技能、知识、资源和目标对事件做出反应并创造新事件一样。

blocks.html_en: In fact, ✈ PIOSEE, a simple and effective decision-making model I covered on the blog, is fundamentally an "event-driven" decision pattern:

sentences.en: In fact, ✈ PIOSEE, a simple and effective decision-making model I covered on the blog, is fundamentally an "event-driven" decision pattern:
sentences.zh: 事实上，✈ PIOSEE，我在博客上介绍的一个简单而有效的决策模型，从根本上来说是一种“事件驱动”的决策模式：

blocks.html_en: • An event happens which you may choose to react, or "subscribe" to ("bind")

sentences.en: An event happens which you may choose to react, or "subscribe" to ("bind")
sentences.zh: 发生事件，您可以选择做出反应，或“订阅”（“绑定”）

blocks.html_en: • You gather information related to the event, or that the event carried directly ("data")

sentences.en: You gather information related to the event, or that the event carried directly ("data")
sentences.zh: 您收集与事件相关的信息，或事件直接携带的信息（“数据”）

blocks.html_en: • Based on this information you decide on the strategy ("callback")

sentences.en: Based on this information you decide on the strategy ("callback")
sentences.zh: 根据此信息，您决定策略（“回调”）

blocks.html_en: • The chosen action is performed ("eval")

sentences.en: The chosen action is performed ("eval")
sentences.zh: 执行所选操作（“eval”）

blocks.html_en: • The results are evaluated and future strategies adjusted as needed ("try/on error")

sentences.en: The results are evaluated and future strategies adjusted as needed ("try/on error")
sentences.zh: 评估结果并根据需要调整未来策略（“尝试/错误”）

blocks.html_en: Beautiful, is it not?

sentences.en: Beautiful, is it not?
sentences.zh: 很漂亮，不是吗？

blocks.html_en: With such an organic approach and Tcl's stable, reliable, non-API-breaking foundation you can develop "timeless" interfaces for modern, platform-native backends, ensuring that your logic stays fast and your UI stays decoupled, regardless of how the underlying OS evolves (or regresses in case of Windows 11). Tcl/Tk code written 20 years ago still runs today. By building your UI with Tcl, you'd be building a tool that would likely one day run on a server on a Lunar colony, with little to no code changes needed.

sentences.en: With such an organic approach and Tcl's stable, reliable, non-API-breaking foundation you can develop "timeless" interfaces for modern, platform-native backends, ensuring that your logic stays fast and your UI stays decoupled, regardless of how the underlying OS evolves (or regresses in case of Windows 11).
sentences.zh: 借助这种有机方法和 Tcl 稳定、可靠、不破坏 API 的基础，您可以为现代平台本机后端开发“永恒”的界面，确保您的逻辑保持快速且 UI 保持解耦，无论底层操作系统如何发展（或在 Windows 11 中退化）。

sentences.en: Tcl/Tk code written 20 years ago still runs today.
sentences.zh: 20 年前编写的 Tcl/Tk 代码今天仍然可以运行。

sentences.en: By building your UI with Tcl, you'd be building a tool that would likely one day run on a server on a Lunar colony, with little to no code changes needed.
sentences.zh: 通过使用 Tcl 构建 UI，您将构建一个可能有一天会在月球殖民地的服务器上运行的工具，几乎不需要更改代码。

blocks.html_en: Python, Tkinter and Tk

sentences.en: Python, Tkinter and Tk
sentences.zh: Python、Tkinter 和 Tk

blocks.html_en: Did you know that Python comes bundled with Tcl/Tk wrapper called "Tkinter"?

sentences.en: Did you know that Python comes bundled with Tcl/Tk wrapper called "Tkinter"?
sentences.zh: 您是否知道 Python 捆绑了名为“Tkinter”的 Tcl/Tk 包装器？

blocks.html_en: Indeed, Python can actually run Tcl code. The problem is — executing Tcl commands inside Python scripts is awkward, but even worse is the fact that for a long time the bundled Tk installation defaulted to the classic, "ugly" widget/font set rather than the Ttk Themed Tk widgets.

sentences.en: Indeed, Python can actually run Tcl code.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Python 实际上可以运行 Tcl 代码。

sentences.en: The problem is — executing Tcl commands inside Python scripts is awkward, but even worse is the fact that for a long time the bundled Tk installation defaulted to the classic, "ugly" widget/font set rather than the Ttk Themed Tk widgets.
sentences.zh: 问题是 - 在 Python 脚本中执行 Tcl 命令很尴尬，但更糟糕的是，很长一段时间以来，捆绑的 Tk 安装默认使用经典的“丑陋”小部件/字体集，而不是 Ttk 主题 Tk 小部件。

blocks.html_en: Namespaces

sentences.en: Namespaces
sentences.zh: 命名空间

blocks.html_en: As with other programming languages, it's always a good idea to avoid polluting the global program scope with functions and variables.

sentences.en: As with other programming languages, it's always a good idea to avoid polluting the global program scope with functions and variables.
sentences.zh: 与其他编程语言一样，避免函数和变量污染全局程序范围始终是个好主意。

blocks.html_en: Tcl was created by John Ousterhout in 1988. For the first nine years of its life (versions 1.0 through 7.6) everything was global: there was exactly one global namespace for procedures, and one global scope for shared variables. Because managing massive codebases with just prefixes was painful, Michael McLennan created a wildly popular object-oriented extension called [incr Tcl] (often stylized as iTcl). It was iTcl that pioneered its own namespace mechanism to isolate classes and methods.

sentences.en: Tcl was created by John Ousterhout in 1988.
For the first nine years of its life (versions 1.0 through 7.6) everything was global: there was exactly one global namespace for procedures, and one global scope for shared variables.
Because managing massive codebases with just prefixes was painful, Michael McLennan created a wildly popular object-oriented extension called [incr Tcl] (often stylized as iTcl).
It was iTcl that pioneered its own namespace mechanism to isolate classes and methods.

blocks.html_en: The Tcl core team adapted the concept, and officially rolled native namespaces (the :: syntax we use today) into the core language with the release of Tcl 8.0 in August 1997.

sentences.en: The Tcl core team adapted the concept, and officially rolled native namespaces (the :: syntax we use today) into the core language with the release of Tcl 8.0 in August 1997.

blocks.html_en: Usually, to achieve isolation in C# or JavaScript, you'd create static classes or namespaces and nest methods and variables inside those. Since Tcl doesn't really support "static classes", the true "Tcl way" to prevent name collisions is through namespaces. However, there is a key distinction between Tcl namespaces and those found in C-style languages:

sentences.en: Usually, to achieve isolation in C# or JavaScript, you'd create static classes or namespaces and nest methods and variables inside those.
Since Tcl doesn't really support "static classes", the true "Tcl way" to prevent name collisions is through namespaces.
sentences.zh: 由于 Tcl 并不真正支持“静态类”，因此防止名称冲突的真正“Tcl 方式”是通过名称空间。

sentences.en: However, there is a key distinction between Tcl namespaces and those found in C-style languages:
sentences.zh: 然而，Tcl 命名空间与 C 风格语言中的命名空间之间存在一个关键区别：

blocks.html_en: • In C#, a namespace is a logical grouping for types (classes, interfaces). You don't "run" or "execute a namespace" (since there's nothing to run), and instead instantiate or reference the types within it

sentences.en: In C#, a namespace is a logical grouping for types (classes, interfaces).
sentences.zh: 在 C# 中，命名空间是类型（类、接口）的逻辑分组。

sentences.en: You don't "run" or "execute a namespace" (since there's nothing to run), and instead instantiate or reference the types within it

blocks.html_en: • In Tcl, a namespace is a container for commands and variables. It is more akin to a JavaScript object used as a module, rather than a simple "logical path"

sentences.en: In Tcl, a namespace is a container for commands and variables.
sentences.zh: 在 Tcl 中，命名空间是命令和变量的容器。

sentences.en: It is more akin to a JavaScript object used as a module, rather than a simple "logical path"
sentences.zh: 它更类似于用作模块的 JavaScript 对象，而不是简单的“逻辑路径”

blocks.html_en: Namespaces were available as a way to "nest" data in Tcl, long before object-oriented programming patterns took over the world of programming. And, in contrast to the C-like languages, where static classes or properties are created at the start of the program and exist until application exit, in Tcl namespaces can be created and deleted at any time, furthering their role as the "ancestors" to the OO pattern in Tcl.

sentences.en: Namespaces were available as a way to "nest" data in Tcl, long before object-oriented programming patterns took over the world of programming.
sentences.zh: 早在面向对象的编程模式接管编程世界之前，命名空间就可以作为在 Tcl 中“嵌套”数据的一种方式。

sentences.en: And, in contrast to the C-like languages, where static classes or properties are created at the start of the program and exist until application exit, in Tcl namespaces can be created and deleted at any time, furthering their role as the "ancestors" to the OO pattern in Tcl.
sentences.zh: 而且，与类 C 语言相反，在类 C 语言中，静态类或属性是在程序启动时创建并一直存在到应用程序退出为止，而 Tcl 中的命名空间可以随时创建和删除，从而进一步发挥了它们作为 Tcl 中 OO 模式“祖先”的作用。

blocks.html_en: Namespaces are created as children of the root namespace, known as :: — and, unlike commands and their arguments which are separated with spaces and tabs, the namespaces and their contents are normally accessed with the same namespace separator, i.e. ::SomeNamespace::somevar. These are known as "fully qualified paths".

blocks.html_en: Shimmering

blocks.html_en: As a result of Tcl being a dual-ported language, and the fact that the underlying C-engine of the interpreter still needs to know the type of data it's dealing with, as a high-level interpreted language Tcl supports type conversion. In Tcl world this is called "shimmering". The funny name is due to the fact that depending on the type of the operation being performed, say — string trim or lreverse — the interpreter has to completely re-generate the internal representation of data, as the former operation happens on data as a string, and the latter must see it as a list. So the underlying data type is constantly flickering or "vibrating" between different states to satisfy the commands you are running.

blocks.html_en: One of the signature features of Tcl is its ability to trace things. You can, for instance, place a trace on a variable or a command, to trigger a script when a certain event occurs with/to it: writing, reading, execution etc. It's commonly used to perform clean-up when a certain variable goes out of scope (like a file reading procedure reaching its end). Or when you want a certain block of code to run each time text changes inside an entry field. Or some UI state variable changes, which might call a series of commands in return etc.

blocks.html_en: As mentioned before, Tcl implements a Copy On Write (CoW) mechanism, so you can pass a dictionary to a command without the program requiring to make a duplicate copy of the data, until it's actually changed. This is a key fact to learn by heart: unlike JS or Python, where you pass references to variables, in Tcl you pass values. Therefore if you change some incoming data inside a Tcl procedure, it will die with that procedure, unless you deliberately export it to the outside scope. This puts another nickel into the "honesty jar" of Tcl — it will only work with the data you gave it, but does support reference counting and provides optimizations to avoid unnecessary memory bloat.

blocks.html_en:
• Use Arrays as a "mini-namespace" for states. For example, you can have a ui_variables() array, and bind its keys to several widgets, without having to deliberately create a separate namespace with flat variables. But what's even more important, and what makes arrays relevant to this day in Tcl, is the fact that arrays don't support copy-on-write. Therefore, to access array elements outside of the scope where the array was created, you must upvar to that scope, to reach the array, and map a local variable to work with its contents, preventing you from accidentally changing a copy instead of the source data
    • Note: if you create an array variable inside a TclOO class, you don't even need to bother with upvar at all! When TclOO creates an "instance" of a class, it generates a dedicated namespace for it. So when you then call $my_Array($key), the TclOO resolver will see the name, check the object's namespace, find the array, and retrieve the value

blocks.html_en:
• Indexing. Here's the difference between passing a name of a namespace into a proc myproc {data_source, dynamic_key} instead of an array reference:
    • Array — set data_source($dynamic_key) "value" — This is native, fast, and easy to read. Just make sure to upvar to the data_source beforehand
    • Namespace — set ${data_source}::${dynamic_key} "value" — This requires double substitution and looks "hacky", whilst also being harder for the interpreter to optimize (and a pain to read!). Note to the experienced Tcl devs: no, shortening this with aliases everywhere is not a great idea either

• Arrays come with functions that namespaces don't have:
    • array names — Instantly get a list of keys using glob patterns: array names ui "button_*". To do this in a namespace, you have to use info vars ${ns}::button_* and then manually strip the namespace prefix off the results. Every time

blocks.html_en: What is the bare minimum needed to make OOP possible? Encapsulation, Inheritance and Polymorphism. In C-like languages, classes are a "compile-time illusion." The CPU has no idea what "objects" are, it only works with memory addresses and jump instructions. To bridge this gap, C++ and C# use two primary mechanisms: Memory Layout and the Virtual Method Table (vtable). On the other hand, Tcl has no vtables, no fixed memory offsets, and no pointers. blocks.html_en: • Tcl commands can also be made to act as "Command Dispatchers", akin to the aforementioned namespace ensembles, so that you could mimic C-like Object.Method(argument) with Tcl's whitespaced syntax object method argument.

blocks.html_en: • Finally, since Tcl is extremely malleable, polymorphism is no issue at all: you can create, destroy and freely redefine commands, namespaces and variables, extend them with new procedures and variables etc.

sentences.en: Finally, since Tcl is extremely malleable, polymorphism is no issue at all: you can create, destroy and freely redefine commands, namespaces and variables, extend them with new procedures and variables etc.
sentences.zh: 最后，由于 Tcl 具有极强的延展性，多态性根本不是问题：您可以创建、销毁和自由地重新定义命令、名称空间和变量，使用新过程和变量等扩展它们。

blocks.html_en: For a long time, all of the parts to implement an OOP-like pattern were already there. All that was missing was a robust abstraction to tie it all together. You can imagine that since in Tcl any first word of a sequence is a command with logic, it can be treated as a custom "object" of sorts. Well, the creators of Tcl realized this as well, and after a long history of various 3rd-party implementations, the official, built-in TclOO class extensions became available in Tcl 8.6 released in December 2012. These gave us oo::class and oo::object commands, effectively providing a way to work with Tcl "OOP-style". However, the "trick" of emulating OOP by using command-routing strings has been possible since the conception of Tcl 1.0 in 1988!

sentences.en: All that was missing was a robust abstraction to tie it all together.
sentences.zh: 所缺少的只是将它们连接在一起的强大抽象。

blocks.html_en: TclOO is essentially a high-performance "bookkeeping" system built on top of Tcl's existing namespace architecture. Instead of changing Tcl's fundamental rules (and breaking backwards compatibility with decades-worth of existing code), the Tcl foundation implemented oo::object in the form of a sophisticated Command Dispatcher (or Command Router).

sentences.en: TclOO is essentially a high-performance "bookkeeping" system built on top of Tcl's existing namespace architecture.
sentences.zh: TclOO本质上是一个建立在Tcl现有命名空间架构之上的高性能“簿记”系统。

sentences.en: Instead of changing Tcl's fundamental rules (and breaking backwards compatibility with decades-worth of existing code), the Tcl foundation implemented oo::object in the form of a sophisticated Command Dispatcher (or Command Router).
sentences.zh: Tcl 基金会没有改变 Tcl 的基本规则（并破坏了与数十年的现有代码的向后兼容性），而是以复杂的命令调度程序（或命令路由器）的形式实现了 oo::object。

blocks.html_en: • Generates a unique string name, like ::oo::Obj42. Tcl can't have "anonymous objects". Every "object" must have a name because it is essentially a command

sentences.en: Generates a unique string name, like ::oo::Obj42.
sentences.zh: 生成唯一的字符串名称，例如::oo::Obj42。

sentences.en: Tcl can't have "anonymous objects".
sentences.zh: Tcl 不能有“匿名对象”。

sentences.en: Every "object" must have a name because it is essentially a command
sentences.zh: 每个“对象”都必须有一个名称，因为它本质上是一个命令

blocks.html_en: • Creates a namespace and a command inside. The new command is the entry point to the "object", and the namespace provides a container for the variables and the methods

sentences.en: Creates a namespace and a command inside.
sentences.zh: 在里面创建一个命名空间和一个命令。

sentences.en: The new command is the entry point to the "object", and the namespace provides a container for the variables and the methods
sentences.zh: 新命令是“对象”的入口点，命名空间为变量和方法提供了容器

blocks.html_en: • Hooks it into a Method Map. Instead of a table of pointers, Tcl stores a list of its method names and their corresponding implementation bodies (which are essentially Tcl procs)

blocks.html_en: And there you have it. A way to implement OOP-like pattern in a language that originally prioritized procedural simplicity. What's also cool about TclOO is that it does really combine the best of both worlds in Tcl:

sentences.en: A way to implement OOP-like pattern in a language that originally prioritized procedural simplicity.
sentences.zh: 一种用最初优先考虑过程简单性的语言实现类 OOP 模式的方法。

sentences.en: What's also cool about TclOO is that it does really combine the best of both worlds in Tcl:
sentences.zh: TclOO 的另一个很酷的地方是它确实结合了 Tcl 中两个世界的优点：

blocks.html_en: • To use variables inside procedures declared within the native Tcl namespaces, you need to "pull" the variables into procs manually with the keyword variable. But since TclOO "objects" store their data and procedures in a private namespace, this boilerplate has been abstracted away: once a variable is declared in the class, it is automatically resolved within the scope of its methods. You get the isolation of a namespace with the ergonomics of a C# class. You can always inspect the name of the namespace the "object" exists in with info object namespace $my_obj, which is also a preferred way to do so, since at any time the command (or the "object") can be renamed manually, which doesn't automatically rename the namespace

sentences.en: To use variables inside procedures declared within the native Tcl namespaces, you need to "pull" the variables into procs manually with the keyword variable.
sentences.zh: 要在本机 Tcl 命名空间中声明的过程中使用变量，您需要使用关键字变量手动将变量“拉”到过程中。

sentences.en: But since TclOO "objects" store their data and procedures in a private namespace, this boilerplate has been abstracted away: once a variable is declared in the class, it is automatically resolved within the scope of its methods.
sentences.zh: 但由于 TclOO“对象”将其数据和过程存储在私有名称空间中，因此该样板已被抽象掉：一旦在类中声明了变量，它就会在其方法的范围内自动解析。

sentences.en: You get the isolation of a namespace with the ergonomics of a C# class.
sentences.zh: 您可以通过 C# 类的人体工程学来隔离命名空间。

sentences.en: You can always inspect the name of the namespace the "object" exists in with info object namespace $my_obj, which is also a preferred way to do so, since at any time the command (or the "object") can be renamed manually, which doesn't automatically rename the namespace
sentences.zh: 您始终可以使用信息对象命名空间 $my_obj 检查“对象”所在的命名空间的名称，这也是这样做的首选方法，因为在任何时候都可以手动重命名命令（或“对象”），这不会自动重命名命名空间

blocks.html_en: • Working with arrays becomes effortless: they are defined inside the namespace the "object" exists in, and the methods are executed within the context of the "object’s" private namespace as well, so you can manipulate arrays directly without the constant upvar gymnastics required in procedural Tcl

sentences.en: Working with arrays becomes effortless: they are defined inside the namespace the "object" exists in, and the methods are executed within the context of the "object’s" private namespace as well, so you can manipulate arrays directly without the constant upvar gymnastics required in procedural Tcl
sentences.zh: 使用数组变得毫不费力：它们是在“对象”所在的命名空间内定义的，并且方法也在“对象”私有命名空间的上下文中执行，因此您可以直接操作数组，而无需过程 Tcl 中所需的常量 upvar 体操

blocks.html_en: • TclOO provides the industry-standard constructor and destructor commands, so you don't need to write you own trace-based logic to free up resources before the destruction of a namespace — simply write a destructor and destroy an "object" with $my_obj destroy.

sentences.en: TclOO provides the industry-standard constructor and destructor commands, so you don't need to write you own trace-based logic to free up resources before the destruction of a namespace — simply write a destructor and destroy an "object" with $my_obj destroy.
sentences.zh: TclOO 提供了行业标准的构造函数和析构函数命令，因此您无需编写自己的基于跟踪的逻辑来在名称空间销毁之前释放资源 — 只需编写析构函数并使用 $my_obj destroy 销毁“对象”即可。

blocks.html_en: • Just like in other languages, you can access the methods of the class within itself with a special call: [my methodname]. In TclOO, if you don't export a method that has a Capitalized name, it will be private, and external callers wouldn't see it. my is the only way to trigger these private behaviors from within the class

sentences.en: Just like in other languages, you can access the methods of the class within itself with a special call: [my methodname].
sentences.zh: 就像在其他语言中一样，您可以通过特殊调用来访问类本身的方法：[my methodname]。

sentences.en: In TclOO, if you don't export a method that has a Capitalized name, it will be private, and external callers wouldn't see it.
sentences.zh: 在 TclOO 中，如果您不导出名称大写的方法，则该方法将是私有的，外部调用者将看不到它。

sentences.en: my is the only way to trigger these private behaviors from within the class
sentences.zh: my 是在班级内触发这些私人行为的唯一方法

blocks.html_en: • Naturally, you still have access to Tcl's powerful tools to redefine everything, so you can create base classes, inherit classes from those, call parent classes' methods and constructors with commands like next or nextto, and change classes at runtime with oo::define. Hell, you can modify the "DNA" of a specific object without affecting its siblings with oo::objdefine!

sentences.en: Naturally, you still have access to Tcl's powerful tools to redefine everything, so you can create base classes, inherit classes from those, call parent classes' methods and constructors with commands like next or nextto, and change classes at runtime with oo::define.
sentences.zh: 当然，您仍然可以使用 Tcl 的强大工具来重新定义所有内容，因此您可以创建基类、从基类继承类、使用 next 或 nextto 等命令调用父类的方法和构造函数，并使用 oo::define 在运行时更改类。

sentences.en: Hell, you can modify the "DNA" of a specific object without affecting its siblings with oo::objdefine!
sentences.zh: 天哪，你可以使用 oo::objdefine 修改特定对象的“DNA”而不影响其兄弟姐妹！

blocks.html_en: While modern frameworks add layers of black box-like abstraction, Tcl keeps things simple. By treating every object as a command and every command as a string, it eliminates the need for complex reflection, serialization, and vtables. It doesn't get in your way because it has fewer ways to do so.

sentences.en: It doesn't get in your way because it has fewer ways to do so.

blocks.html_en: On the bright side — with Tcl you're effectively equipped with a deterministic destruction model, similar to C++'s "delete" or Rust's "ownership", but wrapped in the syntax of a high-level script. There's no background thread "scanning" application memory, so if you don't destroy it, it stays there. But if you do, it’s gone instantly.

sentences.en: There's no background thread "scanning" application memory, so if you don't destroy it, it stays there.

blocks.html_en: All in all, I personally prefer coding in Tcl with TclOO. It "abstracts away" a lot of "Tcl'isms" and house-keeping boilerplate. Besides, the Tcl Core Dev Team did make TclOO an official part of Tcl after all, so maybe there's a good reason for that?

blocks.html_en: People and companies who use it are well aware of what a powerful tool they have on their hands, whilst lack of "casual coder community" reduces visibility of modern Tcl features like TclOO, and ultimately stifles widespread adoption. sentences.en: You know, like improving the language and fixing bugs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如改进语言和修复错误。

sentences.en: They also don't have time to promote Tcl "to the masses" because it makes little sense to do so.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有时间向“大众”推广 Tcl，因为这样做没有什么意义。

sentences.en: People mostly discover Tcl when they stumble upon Tk, and then they either quietly adopt it after reading books and docs, or get spooked by Tcl's unfamiliar command-like nature.
sentences.zh: 人们大多是在偶然发现 Tk 时发现 Tcl 的，然后他们要么在阅读书籍和文档后悄悄采用它，要么被 Tcl 不熟悉的类似命令的性质吓到。

blocks.html_en: As for the users, Tcl is a workhorse in EDA (Electronic Design Automation) and high-end networking, where the people using it are also busy making 💲 💲 💲 with Tcl, without having to justify or advertise their use of it to anyone. When you are designing a microchip with 10 billion transistors, you don't care about "UI trends" or GitHub stars. You care about Zero-Regression and need a language that worked in 1995 and will work in 2045 because the cost of a mistake is a $100 million "tape-out" failure. If anything, I'd argue it's in the interests of large-scale Tcl adopters to stay quiet. Why help the competition discover such a powerful, stable framework when you can just keep making bank in peace?

sentences.en: As for the users, Tcl is a workhorse in EDA (Electronic Design Automation) and high-end networking, where the people using it are also busy making 💲 💲 💲 with Tcl, without having to justify or advertise their use of it to anyone.
sentences.zh: 对于用户来说，Tcl 是 EDA（电子设计自动化）和高端网络领域的主力，使用它的人们也忙着用 Tcl 制作 💲 💲 💲，而无需向任何人证明或宣传他们的使用。

sentences.en: When you are designing a microchip with 10 billion transistors, you don't care about "UI trends" or GitHub stars.
sentences.zh: 当你设计一个拥有 100 亿个晶体管的微芯片时，你并不关心“UI 趋势”或 GitHub 的星星。

sentences.en: You care about Zero-Regression and need a language that worked in 1995 and will work in 2045 because the cost of a mistake is a $100 million "tape-out" failure.
sentences.zh: 您关心零回归，并且需要一种在 1995 年有效并且将在 2045 年有效的语言，因为错误的成本是 1 亿美元的“流片”失败。

sentences.en: If anything, I'd argue it's in the interests of large-scale Tcl adopters to stay quiet.
sentences.zh: 如果说有什么不同的话，我认为保持沉默才符合大规模 Tcl 采用者的利益。

sentences.en: Why help the competition discover such a powerful, stable framework when you can just keep making bank in peace?

blocks.html_en: I on the other hand have no conflict of interest, and want you to try Tcl out. Hence this ginormous, novel-sized article on Tcl 9.0.

sentences.en: I on the other hand have no conflict of interest, and want you to try Tcl out.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我没有利益冲突，并且希望你尝试 Tcl。

sentences.en: Hence this ginormous, novel-sized article on Tcl 9.0.
sentences.zh: 因此才有了这篇关于 Tcl 9.0 的巨著、小说篇幅的文章。

blocks.html_en: Tcl is like the electrical grid. Nobody tweets about the power staying on. They only tweet when it goes out. Because Tcl doesn't break, it doesn't generate the "outrage" or "how to fix it" content that drives the hype cycles of JS or Python. Especially JS. Yeah, JS… On, boy, especially JS…

sentences.en: Tcl is like the electrical grid.
sentences.zh: Tcl就像电网。

sentences.en: Nobody tweets about the power staying on.
sentences.zh: 没有人在推特上说电源仍在继续。

sentences.en: They only tweet when it goes out.
sentences.zh: 他们只在发布时发推文。

sentences.en: Because Tcl doesn't break, it doesn't generate the "outrage" or "how to fix it" content that drives the hype cycles of JS or Python.
sentences.zh: 因为 Tcl 不会崩溃，所以它不会产生推动 JS 或 Python 炒作周期的“愤怒”或“如何修复它”内容。

sentences.en: Especially JS.
sentences.zh: 尤其是JS。

sentences.en: Yeah, JS…
sentences.zh: 是的，JS…

sentences.en: On, boy, especially JS…
sentences.zh: 好吧，男孩，尤其是 JS……

blocks.html_en: Any business can take the Tcl source, bake it into a $500,000 piece of hardware or software, and never mention Tcl again anywhere. There’s no GPL requirement to share source code or proprietary changes to the Tcl interpreter. Thousands of high-end products are "Powered by Tcl" under the hood, and the end-user never knows it.

sentences.en: Any business can take the Tcl source, bake it into a $500,000 piece of hardware or software, and never mention Tcl again anywhere.
sentences.zh: 任何企业都可以采用 Tcl 源代码，将其融入价值 500,000 美元的硬件或软件中，并且永远不会在任何地方再次提及 Tcl。

sentences.en: There’s no GPL requirement to share source code or proprietary changes to the Tcl interpreter.
sentences.zh: 没有 GPL 要求来共享源代码或对 Tcl 解释器进行专有更改。

sentences.en: Thousands of high-end products are "Powered by Tcl" under the hood, and the end-user never knows it.
sentences.zh: 数以千计的高端产品在幕后都是“Powered by Tcl”，而最终用户却永远不知道。

blocks.html_en: Tcl existed, Tcl exists, Tcl will continue to exist. It is over 38 years old now, and it will outlive the vast majority of hyped up languages and frameworks that regularly pop up here and there, trying to reinvent the wheel.

sentences.en: Tcl existed, Tcl exists, Tcl will continue to exist.
sentences.zh: Tcl存在，Tcl存在，Tcl将继续存在。

sentences.en: It is over 38 years old now, and it will outlive the vast majority of hyped up languages and frameworks that regularly pop up here and there, trying to reinvent the wheel.
sentences.zh: 它现在已经有超过 38 年的历史了，它将比绝大多数经常出现、试图重新发明轮子的大肆宣传的语言和框架更长寿。

blocks.html_en: If you go with Tcl, you will essentially adopt the robust and reliable Industrial Architecture of the Fortune 500 tech giants for your own projects, while the rest of the world plays "Framework Musical Chairs", losing their minds and trying to hide their tears from exhaustion.

sentences.en: If you go with Tcl, you will essentially adopt the robust and reliable Industrial Architecture of the Fortune 500 tech giants for your own projects, while the rest of the world plays "Framework Musical Chairs", losing their minds and trying to hide their tears from exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 如果你选择Tcl，你基本上会在自己的项目中采用财富500强科技巨头强大而可靠的工业架构，而世界其他地方却在玩“框架音乐椅”，失去理智，试图隐藏疲惫的眼泪。

blocks.html_en: Practical Tcl/Tk Use Case — Decent Espresso

sentences.en: Practical Tcl/Tk Use Case — Decent Espresso
sentences.zh: 实用的 Tcl/Tk 用例 — Decent Espresso

blocks.html_en: However amazing Tcl/Tk is for automation and systems orchestration, you'll rarely see it openly and deliberately used in consumer products. Which makes the following example even more fascinating.

sentences.en: However amazing Tcl/Tk is for automation and systems orchestration, you'll rarely see it openly and deliberately used in consumer products.
sentences.zh: 无论 Tcl/Tk 在自动化和系统编排方面多么出色，您都很少会看到它在消费产品中公开且有意地使用。

sentences.en: Which makes the following example even more fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这使得下面的例子更加有趣。

blocks.html_en: Decent Espresso, the makers of the famous Decent Espresso DE1 Series coffee machines developed their Decent Espresso Machine software in Tcl/Tk.

sentences.en: Decent Espresso, the makers of the famous Decent Espresso DE1 Series coffee machines developed their Decent Espresso Machine software in Tcl/Tk.
sentences.zh: Decent Espresso 是著名 Decent Espresso DE1 系列咖啡机的制造商，他们使用 Tcl/Tk 开发了 Decent Espresso Machine 软件。

blocks.html_en: Even the Windows version is not packed into an EXE, and instead distributed as a ZIP to be extracted somewhere and launched with the decent.bat file, which in turn executes the main.tcl script with the bundled undrowish standalone Tcl/Tk interpreter:

sentences.en: Even the Windows version is not packed into an EXE, and instead distributed as a ZIP to be extracted somewhere and launched with the decent.bat file, which in turn executes the main.tcl script with the bundled undrowish standalone Tcl/Tk interpreter:
sentences.zh: 即使 Windows 版本也没有打包到 EXE 中，而是作为 ZIP 分发，以便在某处提取并使用 decent.bat 文件启动，该文件又使用捆绑的 undrowish 独立 Tcl/Tk 解释器执行 main.tcl 脚本：

blocks.html_en: undroidwish\undroidwish-win32.exe src\de1plus.tcl -sdlwidth 1280 -sdlheight 800 -name Decent

sentences.en: undroidwish\undroidwish-win32.exe src\de1plus.tcl -sdlwidth 1280 -sdlheight 800 -name Decent

blocks.html_en: But it's the Android version that's special. It can be run with Androwish — Android app which can run GUI Tcl/Tk scripts and interface with mobile device systems and APIs — everything from the accelerometer and compass to Bluetooth. Currently the Android version of the software is the only one that can actually connect to the real espresso machines via Bluetooth, and is used as the main interface for the devices.

sentences.en: But it's the Android version that's special.
sentences.zh: 但 Android 版本比较特别。

sentences.en: It can be run with Androwish — Android app which can run GUI Tcl/Tk scripts and interface with mobile device systems and APIs — everything from the accelerometer and compass to Bluetooth.
sentences.zh: 它可以与 Androwish 一起运行——Android 应用程序可以运行 GUI Tcl/Tk 脚本并与移动设备系统和 API 交互——从加速度计、指南针到蓝牙的一切。

sentences.en: Currently the Android version of the software is the only one that can actually connect to the real espresso machines via Bluetooth, and is used as the main interface for the devices.
sentences.zh: 目前，Android版本的软件是唯一可以通过蓝牙连接到真正的浓缩咖啡机的软件，并用作设备的主界面。

blocks.html_en: "Generic", or platform-agnostic version is also available for those planning to run their Tcl scripts in exotic OSes like Haiku using undroidwish. With Tcl the sky is the limit. If you can port the interpreter somewhere, or even better — to an OS/device with some sort of a display and an API to interface with it, you could run CLI and GUI Tcl scripts with minimum changes.

sentences.en: "Generic", or platform-agnostic version is also available for those planning to run their Tcl scripts in exotic OSes like Haiku using undroidwish.
sentences.zh: 对于那些计划使用 undroidwish 在 Haiku 等奇异操作系统中运行 Tcl 脚本的人来说，也可以使用“通用”或与平台无关的版本。

sentences.en: With Tcl the sky is the limit.
sentences.zh: 有了 Tcl，天空就是极限。

sentences.en: If you can port the interpreter somewhere, or even better — to an OS/device with some sort of a display and an API to interface with it, you could run CLI and GUI Tcl scripts with minimum changes.
sentences.zh: 如果您可以将解释器移植到某个地方，甚至更好 - 移植到具有某种显示器和与之交互的 API 的操作系统/设备，您就可以以最小的更改运行 CLI 和 GUI Tcl 脚本。

blocks.html_en: In 2019 their lead programmer gave a talk directed toward programmers about the Decent Espresso machine, and especially the Tablet App.

sentences.en: In 2019 their lead programmer gave a talk directed toward programmers about the Decent Espresso machine, and especially the Tablet App.
sentences.zh: 2019 年，他们的首席程序员针对 Decent Espresso 机器，特别是平板电脑应用程序向程序员进行了演讲。

blocks.html_en: One of the talking points was: "Surprising ﬁndings how Tcl outperforms competing other programs (in other languages) trying to do similar things" — among those was the fact that Tcl is open source, and provides platform-agnostic UI API, which is flexible enough to build completely customized event-driven interfaces, like those found in Decent Espresso Software. Opting for Tcl means that the whole app is always represented by the source code, which makes it possible to do in-place changes to save time and money. Instead of tweaking it on the tablet, changes can first be done on any of the supported desktop platforms and tested in undrowish, to get the closest representation of how the app would work in Androwish on a real Android tablet.

sentences.en: One of the talking points was: "Surprising ﬁndings how Tcl outperforms competing other programs (in other languages) trying to do similar things" — among those was the fact that Tcl is open source, and provides platform-agnostic UI API, which is flexible enough to build completely customized event-driven interfaces, like those found in Decent Espresso Software.
sentences.zh: 其中一个话题是：“令人惊讶的发现是，Tcl 如何胜过其他试图做类似事情的竞争程序（使用其他语言）”——其中一个事实是 Tcl 是开源的，并提供与平台无关的 UI API，该 API 足够灵活，可以构建完全定制的事件驱动界面，就像 Decent Espresso Software 中的界面一样。

sentences.en: Opting for Tcl means that the whole app is always represented by the source code, which makes it possible to do in-place changes to save time and money.
sentences.zh: 选择 Tcl 意味着整个应用程序始终由源代码表示，这使得可以进行就地更改以节省时间和金钱。

sentences.en: Instead of tweaking it on the tablet, changes can first be done on any of the supported desktop platforms and tested in undrowish, to get the closest representation of how the app would work in Androwish on a real Android tablet.
sentences.zh: 无需在平板电脑上进行调整，而是可以首先在任何受支持的桌面平台上进行更改，并在 undrowish 中进行测试，以获得应用程序在真实 Android 平板电脑上的 Androwish 中如何工作的最接近表示。

blocks.html_en: Why Choose Tcl/Tk?

sentences.en: Why Choose Tcl/Tk?
sentences.zh: 为什么选择Tcl/Tk？

blocks.html_en: Decent Espresso is truly unique because they went with Tcl/Tk in AndroWish for a UI "framework".

sentences.en: Decent Espresso is truly unique because they went with Tcl/Tk in AndroWish for a UI "framework".
sentences.zh: Decent Espresso 确实是独一无二的，因为他们在 AndroWish 中与 Tcl/Tk 一起使用了 UI“框架”。

blocks.html_en: Most device manufacturers would avoid this because:

sentences.en: Most device manufacturers would avoid this because:
sentences.zh: 大多数设备制造商会避免这种情况，因为：

blocks.html_en: • It’s easier to find a React developer than a Tcl one when deciding on a UI framework. To "run" a web app all you need is a device with a browser and access to the local network. This completely negates the "I can't run this on my iPad" problem Decent Espresso have been facing since day 1

sentences.en: It’s easier to find a React developer than a Tcl one when deciding on a UI framework.
sentences.zh: 在决定 UI 框架时，找到 React 开发人员比找到 Tcl 开发人员更容易。

sentences.en: To "run" a web app all you need is a device with a browser and access to the local network.
sentences.zh: 要“运行”网络应用程序，您只需要一台带有浏览器并可以访问本地网络的设备。

sentences.en: This completely negates the "I can't run this on my iPad" problem Decent Espresso have been facing since day 1
sentences.zh: 这完全消除了 Decent Espresso 从第一天起就面临的“我无法在 iPad 上运行这个”问题

blocks.html_en: • Consequently, if you go with web-based tech, you will need to equip your devices with WiFi- or Ethernet-capable network cards or microcontrollers, and establish communion on LAN instead of Bluetooth…

sentences.en: Consequently, if you go with web-based tech, you will need to equip your devices with WiFi- or Ethernet-capable network cards or microcontrollers, and establish communion on LAN instead of Bluetooth…
sentences.zh: 因此，如果您采用基于网络的技术，您将需要为您的设备配备支持 WiFi 或以太网的网卡或微控制器，并在 LAN 而不是蓝牙上建立通信……

blocks.html_en: • …which would make a transition from a LAN-only to a cloud-based solution smoother…

sentences.en: …which would make a transition from a LAN-only to a cloud-based solution smoother…
sentences.zh: ...这将使从仅 LAN 解决方案过渡到基于云的解决方案更加顺利...

blocks.html_en: • …which would, of course, simplify the introduction of vendor locks and paid subscriptions

sentences.en: …which would, of course, simplify the introduction of vendor locks and paid subscriptions
sentences.zh: …当然，这会简化供应商锁定和付费订阅的引入

blocks.html_en: • PROFIT!

sentences.en: PROFIT!
sentences.zh: 利润！

blocks.html_en: Decent Espresso's choice of Tcl/Tk is a middle finger to the entire model of such a "walled garden". It is a local-first architecture where the tablet is a peer to the machine, not a client of a distant server.

sentences.en: Decent Espresso's choice of Tcl/Tk is a middle finger to the entire model of such a "walled garden".
sentences.zh: Decent Espresso 选择 Tcl/Tk 是对这种“围墙花园”整个模式的中指。

sentences.en: It is a local-first architecture where the tablet is a peer to the machine, not a client of a distant server.
sentences.zh: 它是一种本地优先的架构，其中平板电脑是机器的对等方，而不是远程服务器的客户端。

blocks.html_en: Mad. Respect.

sentences.en: Mad.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的。

sentences.en: Respect.
sentences.zh: 尊重。

blocks.html_en: Realistically though, Decent probably uses Tcl/Tk because their lead dev (John Buckman) simply loves the language and the speed of iteration it allows =)

sentences.en: Realistically though, Decent probably uses Tcl/Tk because their lead dev (John Buckman) simply loves the language and the speed of iteration it allows =)
sentences.zh: 但实际上，Decent 可能使用 Tcl/Tk，因为他们的首席开发人员（John Buckman）只是喜欢这种语言及其允许的迭代速度 =)

blocks.html_en: There's a good evidence of that, as he gave a talk on this very topic at the EuroTcl2019 conference. It's essentially the same presentation as the one on the Decent Espresso channel, except at the end he's asked how DE deals with the fact that Android tablets can have wildly different screen resolutions, and Tcl/Tk doesn't really support adaptive rasterized graphics. There, John Buckman confirms that this is a problem, and images need to be "physically" resized first, before Tk can make use of them. Which is a very good explanation of why other companies don't use Tcl/Tk in such a way.

sentences.en: There's a good evidence of that, as he gave a talk on this very topic at the EuroTcl2019 conference.
sentences.zh: 他在 EuroTcl2019 会议上就这个主题发表了演讲，这就是一个很好的证据。

sentences.en: It's essentially the same presentation as the one on the Decent Espresso channel, except at the end he's asked how DE deals with the fact that Android tablets can have wildly different screen resolutions, and Tcl/Tk doesn't really support adaptive rasterized graphics.
sentences.zh: 它本质上与 Decent Espresso 频道上的演示相同，只是最后他被问到 DE 如何处理 Android 平板电脑可能具有截然不同的屏幕分辨率，并且 Tcl/Tk 并不真正支持自适应光栅化图形这一事实。

sentences.en: There, John Buckman confirms that this is a problem, and images need to be "physically" resized first, before Tk can make use of them.
sentences.zh: 在那里，John Buckman 确认这是一个问题，在 Tk 可以使用图像之前，需要先“物理”调整图像大小。

sentences.en: Which is a very good explanation of why other companies don't use Tcl/Tk in such a way.
sentences.zh: 这很好地解释了为什么其他公司不以这种方式使用 Tcl/Tk。

blocks.html_en: Most companies want their machines' UIs to look like "iPhone apps", so they default to web-based tech, which is also very mature. There's an abundance of capable UI frameworks that utilize the browser to do the heavy-lifting and dynamically adapt graphics to different resolutions. So DE had to seriously reinvent the wheel here, and come up with their own tool-set for a skinnable, full-screen UI that would look like a modern app without relying on default Tk widgets. This is impressive, especially considering the challenge of making a window-oriented Tk toolset easy to use for consumers, on a touch-controlled device like an Android tablet.

sentences.en: Most companies want their machines' UIs to look like "iPhone apps", so they default to web-based tech, which is also very mature.
sentences.zh: 大多数公司希望他们的机器的用户界面看起来像“iPhone 应用程序”，因此他们默认使用基于网络的技术，这也非常成熟。

sentences.en: There's an abundance of capable UI frameworks that utilize the browser to do the heavy-lifting and dynamically adapt graphics to different resolutions.
sentences.zh: 有大量功能强大的 UI 框架，它们利用浏览器来完成繁重的工作并动态地使图形适应不同的分辨率。

sentences.en: So DE had to seriously reinvent the wheel here, and come up with their own tool-set for a skinnable, full-screen UI that would look like a modern app without relying on default Tk widgets.
sentences.zh: 因此，DE 必须认真地重新发明轮子，并为可换肤的全屏 UI 开发自己的工具集，使其看起来像一个现代应用程序，而不依赖于默认的 Tk 小部件。

sentences.en: This is impressive, especially considering the challenge of making a window-oriented Tk toolset easy to use for consumers, on a touch-controlled device like an Android tablet.
sentences.zh: 这是令人印象深刻的，特别是考虑到让面向窗口的 Tk 工具集易于消费者在 Android 平板电脑等触摸控制设备上使用的挑战。

sentences.zh: 但如今，无论我多么喜欢 Tcl，我个人在针对这样的用例而使用 Tcl/Tk 之前都会三思而后行。

blocks.html_en: • Since we're not living in the dark ages, we can equip the device with a cheap yet capable microcontroller like ESP32-C5. This would allow it to connect to the local network and use the TCP/IP stack for communication, or even create a WiFi access point with WiFi Direct for other devices to connect to it directly

sentences.en: Since we're not living in the dark ages, we can equip the device with a cheap yet capable microcontroller like ESP32-C5.
sentences.zh: 由于我们还没有生活在黑暗时代，因此我们可以为设备配备便宜但功能强大的微控制器，例如 ESP32-C5。

sentences.en: This would allow it to connect to the local network and use the TCP/IP stack for communication, or even create a WiFi access point with WiFi Direct for other devices to connect to it directly
sentences.zh: 这将允许它连接到本地网络并使用 TCP/IP 堆栈进行通信，甚至可以使用 WiFi Direct 创建一个 WiFi 接入点，以便其他设备直接连接到它

blocks.html_en:
• The same microcontroller, with the help of the powerful real-time OS it comes with (RTOS in case of ESP32) can now do it all:
    1. autonomously manage the device's functions
    2. allow to introduce physical controls like buttons and levers
    3. can offer a simplified interface on a built-in, I2C-connected LCD screen
    4. is capable of setting up a headless HTTP/HTTPS REST or WebSockets API server for remote control

sentences.en: The same microcontroller, with the help of the powerful real-time OS it comes with (RTOS in case of ESP32) can now do it all: autonomously manage the device's functions allow to introduce physical controls like buttons and levers can offer a simplified interface on a built-in, I2C-connected LCD screen is capable of setting up a headless HTTP/HTTPS REST or WebSockets API server for remote control
sentences.zh: 同一个微控制器，借助其附带的强大实时操作系统（ESP32 中的 RTOS）现在可以完成这一切：自主管理设备的功能，允许引入按钮和控制杆等物理控件，可以在内置 I2C 连接的 LCD 屏幕上提供简化的界面，能够设置无头 HTTP/HTTPS REST 或 WebSockets API 服务器以进行远程控制

blocks.html_en: I will also spoil the "secret" which makes DE1 app so smooth on Android, even though technically Tk lacks any form of hardware acceleration. The Decent app runs on Android using AndroWish, which relies on SDLTK. Instead of using the traditional CPU-bound X11 or Win32 drawing calls, SDLTK replaces the entire backend of Tk with the Simple DirectMedia Layer (SDL2), which is hardware-accelerated! By mapping Tk's drawing commands to SDL2 textures, the entire UI gets a performance boost from the GPU. This is why the Decent app can handle high-frequency data visualization on a relatively modest Android tablet.

blocks.html_en: Androwish is an Android app that can run Tcl/Tk scripts inside its own windowing environment. It comes "batteries included", and supports such important packages as sqlite3, tls, Thread and many more, including platform-specific ones like borg, used to communicate with the Android system APIs.

sentences.zh: 它“自带电池”，支持 sqlite3、tls、Thread 等重要包，包括特定于平台的包，如 borg，用于与 Android 系统 API 进行通信。

blocks.html_en: As of May, 2026, Androwish comes with Tcl/Tk 8.6 support only. It's still plenty for performing almost any task you'd use Tcl/Tk for, but do keep in mind that this means that certain commands introduced with the newer versions, like Tcl 9's dict getdef will be unavailable. So plan ahead.

sentences.en: So plan ahead.

blocks.html_en: Lastly, while we're on the topic of running scripts on Android, in addition to those found on the official website, I'd like to share some cool facts and tips about Androwish that aren't obvious, but demonstrate how it's much more than just an "Android Tk wrapper":

sentences.en: Lastly, while we're on the topic of running scripts on Android, in addition to those found on the official website, I'd like to share some cool facts and tips about Androwish that aren't obvious, but demonstrate how it's much more than just an "Android Tk wrapper":
sentences.zh: 最后，当我们讨论在 Android 上运行脚本的主题时，除了在官方网站上找到的内容之外，我还想分享一些关于 Androwish 的酷事实和技巧，这些事实和技巧并不明显，但展示了它不仅仅是一个“Android Tk 包装器”：

blocks.html_en: • After installing Androwish make sure to go to the list of its permissions and give it access to the files on the device. Afterwards, go to: File => Source => Type "sdcard" in the filename field and press "Open" — voia! You can now browse the files on the device and run Tcl scripts from disk

sentences.zh: 安装 Androwish 后，请确保转到其权限列表并授予其访问设备上文件的权限。

sentences.zh: 然后，转到：File => Source => 在文件名字段中输入“sdcard”，然后按“Open” — voia！

sentences.en: You can now browse the files on the device and run Tcl scripts from disk
sentences.zh: 您现在可以浏览设备上的文件并从磁盘运行 Tcl 脚本

blocks.html_en: • By default, Tk apps inside Androwish will simply look like desktop windows running on an Android device. It might be something you're after, but it makes sense to maximize the app to easily make use of the full screen real-estate, as you saw in my Mortgage Calculator Tk showcase.

sentences.en: It might be something you're after, but it makes sense to maximize the app to easily make use of the full screen real-estate, as you saw in my Mortgage Calculator Tk showcase.
sentences.zh: 这可能是您所追求的，但最大化应用程序以轻松利用全屏空间是有意义的，正如您在我的抵押贷款计算器 Tk 展示中看到的那样。

blocks.html_en: • With Androwish, it's possible to create and distribute your own .APK app installers with embedded scripts, which basically act like apps, where Androwish will execute the bundled "main.tcl" file similarly to how a Starkit or a Zipkit would (we'll look at Tcl 9 "Zipkits" further down the post). For this, use the Androwish SDK. The SDK comes bundled with a graphical tool called "bones". The "default" Androwish APK installer is huge (~30MB) because it includes everything. The bones tool allows you to uncheck extensions you aren't using to easily shrink your APK down to ~4-10MB.

blocks.html_en: • You can quickly launch your scripts from the browser or any other app that supports URLs. For that, use a following prefix: androwish:///sdcard/ — and simply append it with the full path to the script you want to run! For example: Documents/mortgage.tcl will trigger an Intent that launches Androwish as a separate Activity, bringing it to the foreground to execute the script. Then, just like with other native apps, when you exit the Tcl script or press the back button (as long as you bind the <Key-Escape> to the exit command), the system stops the current activity and returns you to the previous one — the browser, or a note-taking app etc.

blocks.html_en:
• Androwish comes with the "borg" extension that can be used to call native Android functions: control Bluetooth functionality, send OS notifications (including device vibration and even speech), location information, etc. You really can develop your own, powerful Android CLI/GUI tools with just Tcl/Tk without ever having to touch Android Studio! Just imagine what you're getting for free, entirely open source:
    • No Compilation — you just write a .tcl text file and require common packages
    • Live Testing — save the file, and Androwish runs it instantly. Need to make changes? — Open the file up on the phone/tablet using any text editor and change to your heart's content
    • The "Borg" Bridge — usually, to use Bluetooth or GPS, you'd need to write a lot of Java boilerplate code. Borg is a pre-compiled bridge that lets you stay entirely within the Tcl interpreter and still have access to native system calls
    • And, naturally, as I demonstrated in my Mortgage Calculator demo above — you can have one cross-platform tcl script that could run in almost any OS, including Android, and only package require and trigger Android-specific borg calls upon identifying the platform as "Android" by the presence of this particular package

blocks.html_en: Tcl's Powerful Stackful Coroutines

sentences.en: Tcl's Powerful Stackful Coroutines
