blocks.html_en: A coroutine is a procedure that can "pause" mid-execution, return a value to the caller, and later "resume" exactly where it left off, preserving all local variables and the instruction pointer. If you come from the world of game development, you're probably well aware of coroutines and must've used them at some point to orchestrate scripted events, or to run scripts on a timer. In my game I used coroutines mostly for cutscenes of the Kristie's stage performance sequences, where a single coroutine would act as a "director", triggering systems based on how well the player did on any particular level, with certain events taking place based on the time of day when the performance would take place.

sentences.en: A coroutine is a procedure that can "pause" mid-execution, return a value to the caller, and later "resume" exactly where it left off, preserving all local variables and the instruction pointer.
sentences.zh: 协程是一个可以在执行过程中“暂停”、将值返回给调用者，然后从停止处准确“恢复”的过程，从而保留所有局部变量和指令指针。

sentences.en: If you come from the world of game development, you're probably well aware of coroutines and must've used them at some point to orchestrate scripted events, or to run scripts on a timer.
sentences.zh: 如果您来自游戏开发领域，您可能非常了解协程，并且一定在某些时候使用它们来编排脚本事件，或在计时器上运行脚本。

sentences.en: In my game I used coroutines mostly for cutscenes of the Kristie's stage performance sequences, where a single coroutine would act as a "director", triggering systems based on how well the player did on any particular level, with certain events taking place based on the time of day when the performance would take place.
sentences.zh: 在我的游戏中，我主要将协程用于克里斯蒂舞台表演序列的过场动画，其中单个协程将充当“导演”，根据玩家在任何特定级别上的表现来触发系统，并根据一天中表演发生的时间来发生某些事件。

blocks.html_en: In the world of application development, coroutines are usually employed to break long operations into chunks, like downloading a large file, or processing massive datasets, managing complex state machines, and handling concurrent network requests. They exist because it's not always reasonable to break program execution into actual processing threads, with all the complications that arise with managing shared states etc. So a way to share a single thread between the functions of a program without freezing other operations is needed, and coroutines provide exactly that.

sentences.en: In the world of application development, coroutines are usually employed to break long operations into chunks, like downloading a large file, or processing massive datasets, managing complex state machines, and handling concurrent network requests.
sentences.zh: 在应用程序开发领域，协程通常用于将长操作分解为块，例如下载大文件、处理大量数据集、管理复杂的状态机以及处理并发网络请求。

sentences.en: They exist because it's not always reasonable to break program execution into actual processing threads, with all the complications that arise with managing shared states etc. So a way to share a single thread between the functions of a program without freezing other operations is needed, and coroutines provide exactly that.
sentences.zh: 它们的存在是因为将程序执行分解为实际的处理线程并不总是合理的，管理共享状态等会带来所有的复杂性。因此，需要一种在程序的函数之间共享单个线程而不冻结其他操作的方法，而协程恰恰提供了这种方法。

blocks.html_en: Tcl supports coroutines out of the box. And they can be used almost exactly as in JavaScript, Python or C#: non-blocking when idling, efficient, executed in a queue of other coroutines in the same thread.

sentences.en: Tcl supports coroutines out of the box.
sentences.zh: Tcl 支持开箱即用的协程。

sentences.en: And they can be used almost exactly as in JavaScript, Python or C#: non-blocking when idling, efficient, executed in a queue of other coroutines in the same thread.
sentences.zh: 它们的使用方式几乎与 JavaScript、Python 或 C# 完全相同：空闲时非阻塞、高效、在同一线程中的其他协程队列中执行。

blocks.html_en: This brings the power or "multi-stage" procedures to CLI and desktop apps.

sentences.en: This brings the power or "multi-stage" procedures to CLI and desktop apps.
sentences.zh: 这为 CLI 和桌面应用程序带来了强大的功能或“多阶段”过程。

blocks.html_en: But that's not the whole story.

sentences.en: But that's not the whole story.
sentences.zh: 但这还不是故事的全部。

blocks.html_en: Tcl uses Stackful Coroutines (as do Lua, Erlang and Go).

sentences.en: Tcl uses Stackful Coroutines (as do Lua, Erlang and Go).
sentences.zh: Tcl 使用 Stackful Coroutines（Lua、Erlang 和 Go 也是如此）。

blocks.html_en: In contrast, C++, C#, JavaScript, and Python implement Stackless Coroutines. They rely on the standard LIFO CPU stack, where a function cannot "pause" and remain on the stack. Any procedure must return control to the caller and be popped off. So in these languages the compiler/interpreter actually rewrites coroutine functions into heap-allocated objects because it cannot leave a "hole" in the system stack. And since stackless functions must return to pause, every function in the call chain must be "stackless-aware", that is — marked async.

sentences.en: In contrast, C++, C#, JavaScript, and Python implement Stackless Coroutines.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，C++、C#、JavaScript 和 Python 实现了 Stackless Coroutines。

sentences.en: They rely on the standard LIFO CPU stack, where a function cannot "pause" and remain on the stack.
sentences.zh: 它们依赖于标准 LIFO CPU 堆栈，其中函数无法“暂停”并保留在堆栈上。

sentences.en: Any procedure must return control to the caller and be popped off.
sentences.zh: 任何过程都必须将控制权返回给调用者并弹出。

sentences.en: So in these languages the compiler/interpreter actually rewrites coroutine functions into heap-allocated objects because it cannot leave a "hole" in the system stack.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些语言中，编译器/解释器实际上将协程函数重写为堆分配的对象，因为它不能在系统堆栈中留下“漏洞”。

sentences.en: And since stackless functions must return to pause, every function in the call chain must be "stackless-aware", that is — marked async.
sentences.zh: 由于无堆栈函数必须返回暂停，因此调用链中的每个函数都必须是“无堆栈感知”的，即标记为异步。

blocks.html_en: Sound familiar?

sentences.en: Sound familiar?
sentences.zh: 听起来很熟悉吗？

blocks.html_en: In this regard, Tcl doesn't care about the "C Stack". When you call yield, Tcl snapshots the entire call stack for that coroutine. So you can call Proc A => Proc B => Proc C, and if Proc C calls yield, the entire chain pauses. This approach is incredibly difficult to implement well. To make stackful coroutines work, the authors of the language must write a custom virtual machine that can "detach" and "reattach" segments of memory dynamically. It’s a marvel of software engineering, and in Tcl it's called "NRE" — a Non-Recursive Engine. It was introduced in Tcl 8.6 specifically to solve the problem of pausing execution mid-procedure.

sentences.en: In this regard, Tcl doesn't care about the "C Stack".
sentences.zh: 对此，Tcl并不关心“C Stack”。

sentences.en: When you call yield, Tcl snapshots the entire call stack for that coroutine.
sentences.zh: 当您调用 Yield 时，Tcl 会快照该协程的整个调用堆栈。

sentences.en: So you can call Proc A => Proc B => Proc C, and if Proc C calls yield, the entire chain pauses.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以调用Proc A => Proc B => Proc C，如果Proc C调用yield，整个链就会暂停。

sentences.en: This approach is incredibly difficult to implement well.
sentences.zh: 这种方法很难很好地实施。

sentences.en: To make stackful coroutines work, the authors of the language must write a custom virtual machine that can "detach" and "reattach" segments of memory dynamically.
sentences.zh: 为了使堆栈协程工作，该语言的作者必须编写一个可以动态“分离”和“重新附加”内存段的自定义虚拟机。

sentences.en: It’s a marvel of software engineering, and in Tcl it's called "NRE" — a Non-Recursive Engine.
sentences.zh: 这是软件工程的奇迹，在 Tcl 中它被称为“NRE”——非递归引擎。

sentences.en: It was introduced in Tcl 8.6 specifically to solve the problem of pausing execution mid-procedure.
sentences.zh: 它是在 Tcl 8.6 中引入的，专门用于解决程序中暂停执行的问题。

blocks.html_en: Most modern languages (JS/Python/C#) chose the "Stackless" path because it's easier to bolt onto an existing language, even though it forces the programmer to deal with async/await boilerplate everywhere.

sentences.en: Most modern languages (JS/Python/C#) chose the "Stackless" path because it's easier to bolt onto an existing language, even though it forces the programmer to deal with async/await boilerplate everywhere.
sentences.zh: 大多数现代语言（JS/Python/C#）选择了“Stackless”路径，因为它更容易连接到现有语言，尽管它迫使程序员到处处理异步/等待样板文件。

blocks.html_en: Such "academic" coroutine implementation is objectively one of the most sophisticated in the industry, often compared only to Lua's and Go's. Which explains their common use cases:

sentences.en: Such "academic" coroutine implementation is objectively one of the most sophisticated in the industry, often compared only to Lua's and Go's.
sentences.zh: 这种“学术”协程实现客观上是业界最复杂的实现之一，通常只能与 Lua 和 Go 相比。

sentences.en: Which explains their common use cases:
sentences.zh: 这解释了它们的常见用例：

blocks.html_en: • Lua in Roblox, World of Warcraft, and Lua-based engines (like LÖVE) — In Roblox for instance, every script you write for a part is a coroutine. When you call task.wait(), you are triggering a stackful yield. A game engine cannot afford 10,000 threads. It can afford 10,000 coroutines which occupy a few kilobytes of memory each, and don't require "Context Switching" at the Kernel level. Here's proof

sentences.en: Lua in Roblox, World of Warcraft, and Lua-based engines (like LÖVE) — In Roblox for instance, every script you write for a part is a coroutine.
sentences.zh: Roblox、魔兽世界和基于 Lua 的引擎（如 LÖVE）中的 Lua — 例如，在 Roblox 中，您为某个部分编写的每个脚本都是一个协程。

sentences.en: When you call task.wait(), you are triggering a stackful yield.
sentences.zh: 当您调用task.wait()时，您将触发堆栈yield。

sentences.en: A game engine cannot afford 10,000 threads.
sentences.zh: 游戏引擎无法承受 10,000 个线程。

sentences.en: It can afford 10,000 coroutines which occupy a few kilobytes of memory each, and don't require "Context Switching" at the Kernel level.
sentences.zh: 它可以容纳 10,000 个协程，每个协程占用几千字节的内存，并且不需要内核级别的“上下文切换”。

sentences.en: Here's proof
sentences.zh: 这是证明

blocks.html_en: • Tcl in Cadence, Synopsys, and Siemens Software — as a total surprise to no one, in EDA apps of billion-dollar-valued companies billions of transistors need to be simulated. Tcl's yield implementation allows the simulation to pause a script while the physics engine calculates the electrons, then resume the script exactly where it left off

sentences.zh: Cadence、Synopsys 和西门子软件中的 Tcl — 没有人会感到惊讶，在价值数十亿美元的公司的 EDA 应用程序中，需要模拟数十亿个晶体管。

blocks.html_en: • Go’s in the cloud/server world — Go's success in this area is largely a result of it solving the problem that plagues C# and JavaScript, because… Go has no async and await keywords! It doesn't need them. Go is actually the most advanced in this regard, because it can pause a coroutine at any moment, whereas with Tcl and Lua the code must explicitly say yield to pass the execution over to the next process

sentences.en: Go’s in the cloud/server world — Go's success in this area is largely a result of it solving the problem that plagues C# and JavaScript, because…
sentences.zh: Go 在云/服务器领域——Go 在这一领域的成功很大程度上是因为它解决了困扰 C# 和 JavaScript 的问题，因为……

sentences.en: Go has no async and await keywords!
sentences.zh: Go 没有 async 和 wait 关键字！

sentences.en: It doesn't need them.
sentences.zh: 它不需要它们。

sentences.en: Go is actually the most advanced in this regard, because it can pause a coroutine at any moment, whereas with Tcl and Lua the code must explicitly say yield to pass the execution over to the next process
sentences.zh: Go 实际上在这方面是最先进的，因为它可以随时暂停协程，而使用 Tcl 和 Lua 时，代码必须显式地说yield 将执行传递给下一个进程

blocks.html_en: • (Side-note) In regards to C# in .NET 11 — things are improving somewhat with the new "Runtime Async" approach, where instead of the compiler generating a massive, hideous IAsyncStateMachine state machine struct, starting with .NET 11 it marks the method with a brand new flag. The JIT then compiles it as a new "resumable method". Thus, the updated .NET runtime itself can manage the suspension, which should at least boost overall performance of all async-aware code. But fundamentally C# still is, and will remain stackless for the foreseeable future. So please, don't confuse my talking about this design trade-off with bashing C++ or C# for it! Stackless makes sense for a systems language aimed at maximum efficiency, so such choice is a sensible compromise. Tcl coroutines are more expensive in terms of CPU and memory because they keep a whole stack alive, but they are cheap and convenient for the programmer because you don't have to change your code structure and "color" functions as async all the way up the code chain. C# "coroutines" (Iterators/Async) are cheap for the CPU because they don't hold onto a real OS thread or a full memory stack, but they are awkward for the programmer because they force you to color each function in the chain as async and call await to match

sentences.en: (Side-note) In regards to C# in .NET 11 — things are improving somewhat with the new "Runtime Async" approach, where instead of the compiler generating a massive, hideous IAsyncStateMachine state machine struct, starting with .NET 11 it marks the method with a brand new flag.
sentences.zh: （旁注）关于 .NET 11 中的 C#，通过新的“运行时异步”方法，情况有所改善，从 .NET 11 开始，编译器不再生成大量、丑陋的 IAsyncStateMachine 状态机结构，而是用一个全新的标志来标记该方法。

sentences.en: The JIT then compiles it as a new "resumable method".
sentences.zh: 然后 JIT 将其编译为新的“可恢复方法”。

sentences.en: Thus, the updated .NET runtime itself can manage the suspension, which should at least boost overall performance of all async-aware code.
sentences.zh: 因此，更新后的 .NET 运行时本身可以管理暂停，这至少应该提高所有异步感知代码的整体性能。

sentences.en: But fundamentally C# still is, and will remain stackless for the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上来说，C# 仍然是、并且在可预见的未来仍将保持无堆栈状态。

sentences.en: So please, don't confuse my talking about this design trade-off with bashing C++ or C# for it!
sentences.zh: 所以，请不要将我谈论这种设计权衡与抨击 C++ 或 C# 混为一谈！

sentences.en: Stackless makes sense for a systems language aimed at maximum efficiency, so such choice is a sensible compromise.
sentences.zh: Stackless 对于旨在最大效率的系统语言来说是有意义的，因此这样的选择是一个明智的妥协。

sentences.en: Tcl coroutines are more expensive in terms of CPU and memory because they keep a whole stack alive, but they are cheap and convenient for the programmer because you don't have to change your code structure and "color" functions as async all the way up the code chain.
sentences.zh: Tcl 协程在 CPU 和内存方面更昂贵，因为它们使整个堆栈保持活动状态，但它们对于程序员来说既便宜又方便，因为您不必在代码链上一直以异步方式更改代码结构和“颜色”函数。

sentences.en: C# "coroutines" (Iterators/Async) are cheap for the CPU because they don't hold onto a real OS thread or a full memory stack, but they are awkward for the programmer because they force you to color each function in the chain as async and call await to match
sentences.zh: C#“协程”（迭代器/异步）对于 CPU 来说很便宜，因为它们不保留真正的操作系统线程或完整的内存堆栈，但它们对于程序员来说很尴尬，因为它们迫使您将链中的每个函数着色为异步并调用 wait 来匹配

The nested procedure wait_ms is able to deal with the yield statement as a result of that, triggering the after timer by passing the name of ::fullcoro coroutine as a script to be run after a specified delay, yielding until that timed call, and then returning the execution back to the animated_type proc. Resulting in the "animated type" effect:

sentences.en: In the following example the whole sequence is started as a single coroutine.
sentences.zh: 在以下示例中，整个序列作为单个协程启动。

sentences.en: The nested procedure wait_ms is able to deal with the yield statement as a result of that, triggering the after timer by passing the name of ::fullcoro coroutine as a script to be run after a specified delay, yielding until that timed call, and then returning the execution back to the animated_type proc.

This allows the main thread to remain responsive (handling GUIs or other tasks) while the coroutine waits for I/O.

blocks.html_en: Threading is an advanced topic, and threads should ideally be used only when absolutely necessary due to the added need to control several concurrent instructions taking place in a single app. Parallel programming is notoriously difficult for a variety of reasons: race conditions, deadlocks, threads becoming unresponsive etc.

sentences.zh: 线程是一个高级主题，理想情况下，应仅在绝对必要时使用线程，因为需要控制单个应用程序中发生的多个并发指令。

sentences.en: Parallel programming is notoriously difficult for a variety of reasons: race conditions, deadlocks, threads becoming unresponsive etc.
sentences.zh: 由于多种原因，并行编程是出了名的困难：竞争条件、死锁、线程变得无响应等。

blocks.html_en: These problems are commonly caused by threads sharing the same memory space, where they all have access to the same data — In C++, C#, Java you need to be very careful and employ semaphores to ensure only one thread can access a single piece of data at the same time. When programming for ESP32 I had a fine time using semaphores to provide a safe shared access to the same LCD screen for my animation routines, to avoid the screen crashing due to an on-going I2C command being interrupted mid-way by another instruction.

blocks.html_en: • Shared Memory Containers — primarily TSV (Thread Shared Variables), provided by the Thread package. Unlike a standard C# variable where you point to a memory address, tsv commands are internally protected by mutexes. All you do is call the provided commands from the TSV namespace to get, set or change values, and each operation will be guaranteed to be atomic, automatically managing queuing when several threads try to access or change the same shared variable. TSV variables are not native Tcl variables, you can't put a trace on them for instance. But they do provide certain commands to atomically operate on data as if it were a string, a list, an array, or a keyed list (like a dictionary)

blocks.html_en: • Shared Channels — In C# or C++, you can pass a socket handle to multiple threads. However, if two threads call write() on that socket simultaneously, the data can get interleaved or corrupted at the OS level. You have to wrap the socket in a lock to prevent this. Tcl forces safety by design, so you can't access the same channel from several threads. You need to pass the channel between threads using such commands as thread::transfer, thread::detach and thread::attach

blocks.html_en: For control, by default each thread enters an event loop and can only be controlled via messages. blocks.html_en: If a thread freezes — there's no way to "kill" it. This is because a thread owns an interpreter, so it may have open files (or channels), or be changing a shared variable. If you were to "kill" the OS thread, the Tcl library wouldn't be able to clean up the internal C structures, leading to a corrupted process state or an immediate crash of the entire application. So If your child thread enters an infinite loop like while {1} {}, that thread is "lost" to your application until the process exits. It will sit there consuming 100% of a CPU core, and no thread::send will ever reach it because it never returns to the event loop to check its messages.

blocks.html_en: Such memory efficiency is mostly possible thanks to the complete lack of JIT compilation. C#, Node, Java translate bytecode into machine code at runtime and cache it in a "Code Cache" in RAM. Doing work in 32 threads leads to bloated RAM cache. In contrast, Tcl is strictly a Bytecode Interpreter, written in highly optimized C. It compiles a merged script into internal bytecode once, and then steps through it.

sentences.en: Such memory efficiency is mostly possible thanks to the complete lack of JIT compilation.
sentences.zh: 由于完全没有 JIT 编译，这样的内存效率是可能实现的。

sentences.en: C#, Node, Java translate bytecode into machine code at runtime and cache it in a "Code Cache" in RAM.
sentences.zh: C#、Node、Java 在运行时将字节码转换为机器代码，并将其缓存在 RAM 中的“代码缓存”中。

sentences.en: Doing work in 32 threads leads to bloated RAM cache.
sentences.zh: 在 32 个线程中工作会导致 RAM 缓存膨胀。

sentences.en: In contrast, Tcl is strictly a Bytecode Interpreter, written in highly optimized C.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，Tcl 严格来说是一个字节码解释器，用高度优化的 C 语言编写。

sentences.en: It compiles a merged script into internal bytecode once, and then steps through it.
sentences.zh: 它将合并的脚本编译为内部字节码一次，然后逐步执行它。

blocks.html_en: So all in all, Tcl is hitting almost C levels of memory efficiency while remaining a high-level interpreter.

sentences.en: So all in all, Tcl is hitting almost C levels of memory efficiency while remaining a high-level interpreter.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，Tcl 几乎达到了 C 级别的内存效率，同时仍然是一个高级解释器。

blocks.html_en: High Memory Efficiency Doesn't Imply Maximum Performance

blocks.html_en: Dial back and note how I say "memory efficiency".

blocks.html_en: Tcl was conceived as a "glue" language, not one meant for compute. On a modern multicore CPU, you could use it for heavy math, but it would be a giant waste of CPU power still. It’s much slower in raw execution speed than Rust, C or C#, of course. But no one should use any high-level interpreted language for heavy number-crunching tasks like compression or AI model training/inference anyway.

sentences.en: Tcl was conceived as a "glue" language, not one meant for compute.
sentences.zh: Tcl 被认为是一种“粘合”语言，而不是用于计算的语言。

sentences.en: On a modern multicore CPU, you could use it for heavy math, but it would be a giant waste of CPU power still.
sentences.zh: 在现代多核 CPU 上，您可以使用它来进行繁重的数学计算，但这仍然是对 CPU 功率的巨大浪费。

sentences.en: It’s much slower in raw execution speed than Rust, C or C#, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，它的原始执行速度比 Rust、C 或 C# 慢得多。

sentences.en: But no one should use any high-level interpreted language for heavy number-crunching tasks like compression or AI model training/inference anyway.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，任何人都不应该使用任何高级解释语言来执行繁重的数字运算任务，例如压缩或人工智能模型训练/推理。

sentences.en: 70x performance difference for doing lots of math.

sentences.zh: 即使您在 Tcl 中饱和了 16 个线程，本机 C# 代码的单个核心仍将比所有 16 个 Tcl 线程加起来快近 4.5 倍。

blocks.html_en: Therefore, just how it says in the Tcl source code description, the right way to think of threading in Tcl is not as a rival to C#'s System.Threading.Tasks, or Go’s goroutines, or Rust’s Fearless Concurrency, but rather as a tool for guaranteed UI responsiveness and asynchronous orchestration. Imagine doing a long-running background task — like downloading lots of files or reading/writing to lots of channels/devices in the background. Use threading so your app window doesn't freeze, while being able to query the status of the on-going task to display it on a progress bar. Or, if your Tcl tool runs in the console — draw an ASCII spinner with a coroutine, or continue dispatching tasks while waiting for several child treads to finish their heavy, thread-blocking work and return results using callback messages, the event-driven way.

sentences.en: Therefore, just how it says in the Tcl source code description, the right way to think of threading in Tcl is not as a rival to C#'s System.Threading.Tasks, or Go’s goroutines, or Rust’s Fearless Concurrency, but rather as a tool for guaranteed UI responsiveness and asynchronous orchestration.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如 Tcl 源代码描述中所说，将 Tcl 中的线程视为 C# 的 System.Threading.Tasks、Go 的 goroutine 或 Rust 的无畏并发的竞争对手，而不是作为保证 UI 响应能力和异步编排的工具。

sentences.en: Imagine doing a long-running background task — like downloading lots of files or reading/writing to lots of channels/devices in the background.
sentences.zh: 想象一下执行一个长时间运行的后台任务 - 例如下载大量文件或在后台读取/写入大量通道/设备。

sentences.en: Use threading so your app window doesn't freeze, while being able to query the status of the on-going task to display it on a progress bar.
sentences.zh: 使用线程，这样您的应用程序窗口就不会冻结，同时能够查询正在进行的任务的状态以将其显示在进度栏上。

sentences.en: Or, if your Tcl tool runs in the console — draw an ASCII spinner with a coroutine, or continue dispatching tasks while waiting for several child treads to finish their heavy, thread-blocking work and return results using callback messages, the event-driven way.
sentences.zh: 或者，如果您的 Tcl 工具在控制台中运行 — 使用协程绘制 ASCII 旋转器，或者继续分派任务，同时等待多个子线程完成繁重的线程阻塞工作并使用回调消息（事件驱动的方式）返回结果。

blocks.html_en: Tcl is about concurrency (doing many tasks at once), and not parallelism (doing one big task faster). Still, if you really want to reach C-like performance-levels straight from Tcl, there is a solution…

sentences.en: Tcl is about concurrency (doing many tasks at once), and not parallelism (doing one big task faster).
sentences.zh: Tcl 是关于并发（一次执行许多任务），而不是并行（更快地执行一项大任务）。

sentences.en: Still, if you really want to reach C-like performance-levels straight from Tcl, there is a solution…

blocks.html_en: You can embed C code into your Tcl scripts.

sentences.en: You can embed C code into your Tcl scripts.

blocks.html_en: Script-Embedded C? Script-Embedded C!

sentences.en: Script-Embedded C!

blocks.html_en: Tcl has a package called critcl — Compiled Runtime for Tcl — which allows you to embed C code directly inside your Tcl scripts. And it compiles it on the fly, once. You write a snippet of C, and Tcl handles the compilation, linking, and loading automatically. This, for instance, allows accessing Tcl_Obj internal representation struct, which the C code sees as raw bytes in memory. NaviServer, a web server written in Tcl/C, is designed around this very concept.

sentences.en: Tcl has a package called critcl — Compiled Runtime for Tcl — which allows you to embed C code directly inside your Tcl scripts.
sentences.zh: Tcl 有一个名为 critcl 的包（Tcl 编译运行时），它允许您将 C 代码直接嵌入到 Tcl 脚本中。

sentences.en: And it compiles it on the fly, once.
sentences.zh: 它会即时编译一次。

sentences.en: You write a snippet of C, and Tcl handles the compilation, linking, and loading automatically.
sentences.zh: 您编写一段 C 代码，Tcl 会自动处理编译、链接和加载。

sentences.en: This, for instance, allows accessing Tcl_Obj internal representation struct, which the C code sees as raw bytes in memory.
sentences.zh: 例如，这允许访问 Tcl_Obj 内部表示结构，C 代码将其视为内存中的原始字节。

sentences.en: NaviServer, a web server written in Tcl/C, is designed around this very concept.
sentences.zh: NaviServer 是一个用 Tcl/C 编写的 Web 服务器，就是围绕这个概念而设计的。

blocks.html_en: As a quick demo — in "raw" Tcl, a loop for calculating a Mandelbrot set or a large Fibonacci sequence is slow because every iteration is an interpreted command. With critcl, you can write a performance-critical loop in C, and it behaves like a native Tcl command.

sentences.en: As a quick demo — in "raw" Tcl, a loop for calculating a Mandelbrot set or a large Fibonacci sequence is slow because every iteration is an interpreted command.
sentences.zh: 作为一个快速演示 - 在“原始”Tcl 中，用于计算 Mandelbrot 集或大型 Fibonacci 序列的循环很慢，因为每次迭代都是解释命令。

sentences.en: With critcl, you can write a performance-critical loop in C, and it behaves like a native Tcl command.
sentences.zh: 使用 critcl，您可以用 C 语言编写性能关键的循环，其行为类似于本机 Tcl 命令。

blocks.html_en: With this, you'd essentially be creating a DLL/Shared Object on the fly. You can even embed C++ code with critcl::config language c++ — otherwise, the workflow remains the same.

sentences.en: With this, you'd essentially be creating a DLL/Shared Object on the fly.
sentences.zh: 这样，您实际上就可以动态创建 DLL/共享对象。

sentences.en: You can even embed C++ code with critcl::config language c++ — otherwise, the workflow remains the same.
sentences.zh: 您甚至可以使用 critcl::config 语言 c++ 嵌入 C++ 代码 — 否则，工作流程保持不变。

blocks.html_en: Of course, it's not all "write and forget" as critcl does require a C compiler (gcc or clang) to be present on the machine the first time the script runs. So if you distribute this to a user without a compiler, it fails. The on-the-fly compilation is a development feature. It's meant to give devs the ability to have an all-in-one Tcl script for prototyping. Once the code is finished, you would bake it into a binary. So you'd use critcl to generate a shared library (.dll on Windows, .so on Linux) on your machine. Then distribute that library alongside your script without having to change the script itself:

sentences.en: Of course, it's not all "write and forget" as critcl does require a C compiler (gcc or clang) to be present on the machine the first time the script runs.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不全是“写了就忘记”，因为 critcl 确实需要在脚本第一次运行时机器上存在 C 编译器（gcc 或 clang）。

sentences.en: So if you distribute this to a user without a compiler, it fails.

sentences.en: The on-the-fly compilation is a development feature.

sentences.en: It's meant to give devs the ability to have an all-in-one Tcl script for prototyping.

sentences.en: Once the code is finished, you would bake it into a binary.
sentences.zh: 代码完成后，您可以将其烘焙成二进制文件。

sentences.en: So you'd use critcl to generate a shared library (.dll on Windows, .so on Linux) on your machine.
sentences.zh: 因此，您可以使用 critcl 在计算机上生成共享库（Windows 上为 .dll，Linux 上为 .so）。

sentences.en: Then distribute that library alongside your script without having to change the script itself:

Unless you really know your way around C or C++, and are disciplined and motivated enough to jump though hoops to directly work with Tcl runtime memory structures, you should probably look for another way to supplement your Tcl apps with the ability to do heavy math.

sentences.en: Unless you really know your way around C or C++, and are disciplined and motivated enough to jump though hoops to directly work with Tcl runtime memory structures, you should probably look for another way to supplement your Tcl apps with the ability to do heavy math.
sentences.zh: 除非您真的了解 C 或 C++，并且有足够的纪律和动力去跳过障碍直接使用 Tcl 运行时内存结构，否则您可能应该寻找另一种方法来补充您的 Tcl 应用程序进行繁重的数学计算的能力。

blocks.html_en: Recall that Tcl is a versatile "glue" language for GUI and CLI apps. So why not glue it to something else, written in a modern, managed language, much better suited for a role of a versatile "powerful calculator", while your Tcl UI does what it is meant to — manage and display.

sentences.en: So why not glue it to something else, written in a modern, managed language, much better suited for a role of a versatile "powerful calculator", while your Tcl UI does what it is meant to — manage and display.

blocks.html_en: I compile my C# apps into native code using BFlat.

sentences.en: I compile my C# apps into native code using BFlat.
sentences.zh: 我使用 BFlat 将 C# 应用程序编译为本机代码。

blocks.html_en: Bflat produces portable executables which don't require .NET to be installed on the target platform. With an added bonus of being able to reach C-level performance without having to actually use C or C++, while retaining access to C#'s powerful threading capabilities and its garbage collector! And the resulting binaries are tiny thanks to zero .NET bloat. In fact, you don't even need the .NET runtime or .NET SDK installed on the build system at all, as BFlat comes with precompiled versions of common dependencies. You just write your C# code and compile it with BFlat like you would with C++ and clang++. And then run it anywhere as a self-contained portable executable for Windows, or a binary with minimal dependencies (standard libc) that runs across almost any Linux distro. You can even build binaries for Android!

sentences.en: Bflat produces portable executables which don't require .NET to be installed on the target platform.
sentences.zh: Bflat 生成可移植的可执行文件，不需要在目标平台上安装 .NET。

sentences.en: With an added bonus of being able to reach C-level performance without having to actually use C or C++, while retaining access to C#'s powerful threading capabilities and its garbage collector!
sentences.zh: 额外的好处是无需实际使用 C 或 C++ 即可达到 C 级别的性能，同时保留对 C# 强大的线程功能及其垃圾收集器的访问！

sentences.zh: 事实上，您甚至根本不需要在构建系统上安装 .NET 运行时或 .NET SDK，因为 BFlat 附带了常见依赖项的预编译版本。

sentences.en: You just write your C# code and compile it with BFlat like you would with C++ and clang++.
sentences.zh: 您只需编写 C# 代码并使用 BFlat 对其进行编译，就像使用 C++ 和 clang++ 一样。

sentences.en: And then run it anywhere as a self-contained portable executable for Windows, or a binary with minimal dependencies (standard libc) that runs across almost any Linux distro.
sentences.zh: 然后将其作为适用于 Windows 的自包含可移植可执行文件在任何地方运行，或者以最小依赖项（标准 libc）运行在几乎所有 Linux 发行版上的二进制文件。

A non-bloated, tiny, AoT-compiled C# binary that carries its own garbage collector and runtime with a tiny footprint. Scandalous!

blocks.html_en: Then, for a 100% cross-platform tool package I would compile 2 more binaries — for Linux and macOS — and place those into the bin/ subfolder next to my script. My Tcl "Glue" app would then discover those and execute the appropriate binary depending on the detected platform. As a final accord, I could go even further and pack the whole tool into a standalone binary, making good use of the Zipfs filesystem Tcl 9.0 supports, to bundle the compiled C# binaries inside. These would then get extracted into a directory (bin/ or system tmp/) and spawned as child processes.

blocks.html_en: When Christian Werner started the AndroWish project, he had to deal with the fact that Android apps are distributed as .apk files, which are technically just renamed ZIP archives. For Tcl to run on Android, the interpreter had to be able to somehow "reach into its own APK" to find its library scripts, images, and extensions. To solve this, Christian wrote a C-level Virtual File System (VFS) driver that allowed Tcl to treat a ZIP archive as a live directory. The new driver was robust enough because it didn't rely on complex external database engines and used the zlib already present in the core, plus a minimal C-wrapper to navigate the ZIP directory structure. This code was developed for AndroWish and its desktop sibling undroidwish, before finally being merged into the official Tcl core.

blocks.html_en: For decades Tclkits were available as self-contained executables that bundled the Tcl interpreter, the Tk toolkit, and a virtual filesystem (VFS) into one file, to be used as a portable runtime for running Tcl/Tk scripts. A typical Tclkit uses the Metakit embedded database or a similar technology to provide the VFS. When you run a Tclkit, it mounts this internal database as a filesystem (usually as //zvfs/ or lib/tcl), allowing the script to access bundled packages as if they were on a physical disk. Tclkits served the Tcl developers well, but are now being superseded by the native zip-based features.

blocks.html_en: "GUI-starved" Python developers are well familiar with developing Web Apps using Flask or Bottle, where Python acts a "headless" server that serves pages viewable in any browser. Tcl can do the same using the Wapp framework. Except unlike many Python frameworks that require a separate production server (like Gunicorn or uWSGI) to be secure/stable, Wapp is designed to be production-ready out of the box with only using Tcl’s robust internal socket handling or via CGI/SCGI.

sentences.en: Key features of Wapp:

blocks.html_en: • Wapp is a single-file framework. Just as SQLite is a single-file database, Wapp aims to be a single "wapp.tcl" file that provides the basic functionality expected from a web app. So a complete app is a single file of Tcl

sentences.en: Wapp is a single-file framework.
sentences.zh: Wapp 是一个单文件框架。

sentences.en: Just as SQLite is a single-file database, Wapp aims to be a single "wapp.tcl" file that provides the basic functionality expected from a web app.

sentences.zh: 所以一个完整的应用程序是一个 Tcl 文件

blocks.html_en: • If needed, the web interface can be made accessible from anywhere on the network, which is one of the main benefits of this approach, compared to the purely local CLI/GUI deployment

blocks.html_en: You, too, can deploy a web app with Tcl, as small as a one-file, cross-platform Tcl script. Download the latest wapp.tcl, then include it in your scripts either with the source command, or by turning it into a custom .tm module to include with package require. Done! You've got a reliable and secure Web Framework that includes a built-in Application Server for cases when you require a web-based interface for your Tcl apps.

blocks.html_en: Combine Wapp with a lightweight JavaScript html extension library like htmx, add a couple of lines of css, and you've got yourself an performant, secure, low-overhead modern Hypermedia Driven Application, while writing just a handful of Tcl procedures and 0 lines of JavaScript.

blocks.html_en: BTW, if you think this is the only "correct" approach to making modern apps with interfaces — think again. A web browser is a heavily sandboxed environment. If you spend too much time polishing web apps for the web, you might miss the power of Tcl/Tk’s native GUI capabilities like real-time asynchronous feedback. Use Wapp if the "web-based" requirement is a hard necessity for remote access, or when making the UIs to be easily accessible from mobile devices. If you just need a UI for a local tool, don't overcomplicate and "overly-abstract" things, and stay with Tk. After all, it is also cross-platform by design.

sentences.en: To round out my Tcl/Tk overview, here are a few notable facts I’ve gathered along the way.

blocks.html_en: "WebAssembly From a Parallel Universe"

sentences.en: "WebAssembly From a Parallel Universe"
sentences.zh: 《来自平行宇宙的 WebAssembly》

blocks.html_en: The tech industry currently views WebAssembly (Wasm) as the ultimate solution for running untrusted code at near-native speeds within a secure sandbox. Whether in a browser or a server-side WASI environment, Wasm’s primary value proposition is its isolation.

sentences.en: The tech industry currently views WebAssembly (Wasm) as the ultimate solution for running untrusted code at near-native speeds within a secure sandbox.
sentences.zh: 目前，科技行业将 WebAssembly (Wasm) 视为在安全沙箱中以接近本机的速度运行不受信任代码的终极解决方案。

sentences.en: Whether in a browser or a server-side WASI environment, Wasm’s primary value proposition is its isolation.
sentences.zh: 无论是在浏览器还是服务器端 WASI 环境中，Wasm 的主要价值主张是其隔离性。

blocks.html_en: Believe it or not, but Tcl developers have had access to robust, high-level sandboxing since the early 90s. While Wasm isolates at the instruction level, Tcl isolates at the logical level through "Safe Interpreters."

sentences.en: Believe it or not, but Tcl developers have had access to robust, high-level sandboxing since the early 90s.
sentences.zh: 不管你相信与否，Tcl 开发人员自 90 年代初以来就可以使用强大的高级沙箱。

sentences.en: While Wasm isolates at the instruction level, Tcl isolates at the logical level through "Safe Interpreters."
sentences.zh: Wasm 在指令级别进行隔离，而 Tcl 通过“安全解释器”在逻辑级别进行隔离。

blocks.html_en: To secure a script in Tcl all you need to is spawn a child interpreter and limit its capabilities. By default, a "safe" interpreter is born even without the ability to touch the file system, open network sockets, or load external libraries. You can then extend these permissions, and hide or expose commands as you see fit.

sentences.en: To secure a script in Tcl all you need to is spawn a child interpreter and limit its capabilities.
sentences.zh: 为了保护 Tcl 中的脚本，您需要生成一个子解释器并限制其功能。

sentences.en: By default, a "safe" interpreter is born even without the ability to touch the file system, open network sockets, or load external libraries.
sentences.zh: 默认情况下，即使没有能力接触文件系统、打开网络套接字或加载外部库，“安全”解释器也会诞生。

sentences.en: You can then extend these permissions, and hide or expose commands as you see fit.
sentences.zh: 然后，您可以扩展这些权限，并根据需要隐藏或公开命令。

blocks.html_en: Tcl is known to be a great choice for the development of Domain Specific Languages (DSLs).

blocks.html_en: Technically, Tcl is not so much a "language" in the traditional sense, but a command-processing engine. As you now know, Tcl loops, variable assignments, and conditional logic are all commands followed by arguments. So you can develop whole ensembles of commands your particular business needs, and run those within a Tcl's safe interpreter, ultimately ending up with a completely customized Tcl interactive session.

blocks.html_en: If you define a procedure called unknown it is called with a Tcl list representing arguments of every command Tcl tried to execute, but failed because the command name was not defined. You can do what you like with it, and return a value, or raise an error. If you just return a value, the command will appear to work even if unknown to Tcl, and the return value returned by unknown will be used as return value of the not defined command. Add this to uplevel and upvar, and the language itself that's almost syntax free, and what you get is an impressive environment for Domain Specific Languages development. Tcl has almost no syntax, like Lisp and FORTH, but there are different ways to have no syntax. Tcl looks like a configuration file by default:

blocks.html_en: Why Is Doing Math in Tcl So Awkward?

sentences.en: Why Is Doing Math in Tcl So Awkward?

blocks.html_en: I'm fairly certain when you start learning Tcl you'll get annoyed by the fact that expr must be used to evaluate any math expression. Then you will learn that the expressions themselves must to be placed within the curly braces {} to prevent the Tcl interpreter from substituting the variables before they reach the expr command. Which will lead to a realization that expr acts as its own "mini-compiler" on the whole {expression} no less. It looks inside the braced block, finds the dollar signs and the nested command blocks, and then performs variable lookups and math in one optimized step, finally providing a good explanation for why math is done that way.

blocks.html_en: As for the "dreaded braces" — without them, Tcl interpreter converts everything to a string first, then expr converts it back to a number, which wastes CPU cycles. With braces {}, the internal Tcl_Obj stays a numeric type, but most importantly — bracing prevents "double substitution." If a variable contained something malicious like [exec rm -rf /], a braced expr would treat it as a string/error, whereas an unbraced one might actually execute it. Think of it as an "SQL Injection". A more detailed example can be found below, in the section on Security.

sentences.en: Tcl 9.0 — Strict, Honest and Reliable

blocks.html_en: I previously mentioned that Tcl 9.0 is surprisingly honest and strict for an interpreted language. Consider the following scenario: you have a text document or a Tcl script saved as UTF-8 with a BOM (Byte Order Mark). BOM is a "magic number" at the very beginning of a text file, which was designed to solve several problems that arose when the world moved from ASCII to Unicode. Nowadays, unless you need to work with really old software, there's usually no need to encode UTF files with BOM. But what matters right now is that the BOM itself is technically a Zero-Width No-Break Space — U+FEFF.

blocks.html_en: • Tcl 9 treats the file as a stream of data "as is", without lying to you, to avoid changing the contents in an unexpected way. If the first character is a U+FEFF, Tcl assumes that if it exists in your file, you intended for it to be there. It refuses to curate your data for you. If you then try to append something to the beginning of the contents of the variable (even just a single space), it will be added before the U+FEFF symbol. If you then save this file and try executing it as a Tcl script, Tcl will return an error, because it will skip the space, as it does with all whitespace normally, stumble upon the BOM symbol and try to look it up as a command. And since command with such a name doesn't exist, the program will crash. Here's what such an "appended" file looked like in my IDE:

blocks.html_en:
The extension provides access to the Windows API at two levels. A direct interface to the supported Windows API is provided where the Tcl commands directly map to Windows functions as described in Microsoft Windows SDK. The recommended interface is a higher level interface that is more convenient, powerful and much easier to use than the raw Windows API.

In combination with the built-in facilities in Tcl, TWAPI makes it possible to write a wide variety of Windows applications ranging from desktop applications to web servers running as Windows services

blocks.html_en: I own a perpetual license for Adobe Creative Suite 6 Production Premium. Yes, the CS6 one, released in 2012. It covers all of my media production needs for video, audio and image production and manipulation, allowing me to dodge Adobe's Creative Cloud subscription trap. The problem is that the last version of the Adobe Camera RAW plug-in compatible with the CS6 suite is version 9.1.1 from 2015. It's a perfectly functional and extremely capable tool for working with RAW images, but naturally, it doesn't support RAW files coming from cameras released after 2015.

blocks.html_en: It would be perfect if not for an unfortunate omission — there's no option to preserve the original file creation or modification dates when exporting DNGs! A single shoot could last for hours or even days, and being able to organize the files based on the their filesystem timestamps is just too valuable.

blocks.html_en: On Nullable Types

sentences.en: On Nullable Types
sentences.zh: 关于可空类型

blocks.html_en: Tony Hoare introduced Null references in ALGOL W back in 1965 "simply because it was so easy to implement". He calls it a "Billion Dollar Mistake" because of the decades of system crashes it caused.

sentences.en: Tony Hoare introduced Null references in ALGOL W back in 1965 "simply because it was so easy to implement".
sentences.zh: Tony Hoare 早在 1965 年就在 ALGOL W 中引入了 Null 引用，“只是因为它很容易实现”。

sentences.en: He calls it a "Billion Dollar Mistake" because of the decades of system crashes it caused.
sentences.zh: 他称其为“十亿美元的错误”，因为它导致了数十年的系统崩溃。

blocks.html_en: In C++, a null is a literal zero in a pointer register. In Tcl and JavaScript, for example, "null" is just another state inside a much larger, more complex "Object" or "Command" structure.

sentences.en: In C++, a null is a literal zero in a pointer register.
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中，空值是指针寄存器中的文字零。

sentences.en: In Tcl and JavaScript, for example, "null" is just another state inside a much larger, more complex "Object" or "Command" structure.
sentences.zh: 例如，在 Tcl 和 JavaScript 中，“null”只是更大、更复杂的“对象”或“命令”结构中的另一种状态。

blocks.html_en: And yet JavaScript somehow allows to check if a certain variable is null. How? It's a "charade." An undefined or null is actually a unique memory constant that the JS Engine’s "Command Router" knows how to handle. It’s a specific "Data type that represents nothingness." With this, JavaScript tries to emulate the "null" experience of C++ but ends up with a confusing null vs undefined mess. Those of us with a web development background know this too well. Strictly speaking, null was intended to represent "the intentional absence of an object," while undefined represents "the absence of a value. Did you know that?

sentences.en: And yet JavaScript somehow allows to check if a certain variable is null.
sentences.zh: 然而 JavaScript 却以某种方式允许检查某个变量是否为空。

sentences.en: How?
sentences.zh: 如何？

sentences.en: It's a "charade."
sentences.zh: 这是一场“猜谜游戏”。

sentences.en: An undefined or null is actually a unique memory constant that the JS Engine’s "Command Router" knows how to handle.
sentences.zh: 未定义或 null 实际上是 JS 引擎的“命令路由器”知道如何处理的唯一内存常量。

sentences.en: It’s a specific "Data type that represents nothingness."
sentences.zh: 它是一种特定的“代表虚无的数据类型”。

sentences.en: With this, JavaScript tries to emulate the "null" experience of C++ but ends up with a confusing null vs undefined mess.
sentences.zh: 这样，JavaScript 尝试模拟 C++ 的“null”体验，但最终会出现令人困惑的 null 与未定义的混乱。

sentences.en: Those of us with a web development background know this too well.
sentences.zh: 我们这些有网络开发背景的人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: Strictly speaking, null was intended to represent "the intentional absence of an object," while undefined represents "the absence of a value.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，null 旨在表示“故意不存在某个对象”，而 undefined 则表示“不存在值”。

sentences.en: Did you know that?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

blocks.html_en: At the same time, in Tcl the "nullability" you see in other languages is handled by existence. You don't check if a variable is null since it makes no sense, as it. You check if it exists in the namespace: info exists varName, or if its string length is zero.

sentences.en: At the same time, in Tcl the "nullability" you see in other languages is handled by existence.
sentences.zh: 同时，在 Tcl 中，您在其他语言中看到的“可空性”是通过存在来处理的。

sentences.en: You don't check if a variable is null since it makes no sense, as it.
sentences.zh: 您不检查变量是否为空，因为它没有意义。

sentences.en: You check if it exists in the namespace: info exists varName, or if its string length is zero.
sentences.zh: 您检查它是否存在于名称空间中： info 存在 varName，或者它的字符串长度是否为零。

blocks.html_en: Tcl doesn't pretend to have nulls, and instead only has states on Storage (Existence) and Content (The String):

sentences.en: Tcl doesn't pretend to have nulls, and instead only has states on Storage (Existence) and Content (The String):
sentences.zh: Tcl 不会假装有空值，而是仅具有存储（存在）和内容（字符串）上的状态：

blocks.html_en: • Existence: info exists varName — is is even there?

sentences.en: Existence: info exists varName — is is even there?
sentences.zh: 存在：信息存在 varName — 是否存在？

blocks.html_en: • Content: if {$varName eq ""} ... — OK, but is it empty?

sentences.en: Content: if {$varName eq ""} ... — OK, but is it empty?
sentences.zh: 内容： if {$varName eq ""} ... — 好的，但是它是空的吗？

blocks.html_en: In Tcl, if you want a "null," you use an empty string "". Because Tcl automates the conversion between strings and other types (integers, lists), an empty string is the only "logical null." If you try to do math on an empty string, Tcl doesn't give you 0 or NaN and instead throws an error because an empty string is not a valid operand.

sentences.en: In Tcl, if you want a "null," you use an empty string "".
sentences.zh: 在 Tcl 中，如果您想要“null”，则可以使用空字符串“”。

sentences.en: Because Tcl automates the conversion between strings and other types (integers, lists), an empty string is the only "logical null."
sentences.zh: 因为 Tcl 自动执行字符串和其他类型（整数、列表）之间的转换，所以空字符串是唯一的“逻辑 null”。

sentences.en: If you try to do math on an empty string, Tcl doesn't give you 0 or NaN and instead throws an error because an empty string is not a valid operand.
sentences.zh: 如果您尝试对空字符串进行数学运算，Tcl 不会给出 0 或 NaN，而是会抛出错误，因为空字符串不是有效的操作数。

blocks.html_en: In a way, Tcl avoids the "null pointer exception" by simply refusing to acknowledge that a pointer can be a value in the first place, and forces you to be more explicit about your data's existence.

sentences.en: In a way, Tcl avoids the "null pointer exception" by simply refusing to acknowledge that a pointer can be a value in the first place, and forces you to be more explicit about your data's existence.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，Tcl 通过简单地拒绝承认指针可以是一个值来避免“空指针异常”，并迫使您更明确地了解数据的存在。

blocks.html_en: Limitations (and "Quirks")

sentences.en: Limitations (and "Quirks")
sentences.zh: 限制（和“怪癖”）

blocks.html_en: Tcl is not perfect. Its command nature, and the simplicity of its syntax shift the burden of correctness from the compiler to the developer’s discipline. In languages like JavaScript or PHP, the distinction between data and code is enforced by the interpreter. In Tcl, because everything is a string, you are the interpreter.

sentences.en: Tcl is not perfect.
sentences.zh: Tcl并不完美。

sentences.en: Its command nature, and the simplicity of its syntax shift the burden of correctness from the compiler to the developer’s discipline.
sentences.zh: 它的命令性质和语法的简单性将正确性的负担从编译器转移到了开发人员的纪律上。

sentences.en: In languages like JavaScript or PHP, the distinction between data and code is enforced by the interpreter.
sentences.zh: 在 JavaScript 或 PHP 等语言中，数据和代码之间的区别是由解释器强制执行的。

sentences.en: In Tcl, because everything is a string, you are the interpreter.
sentences.zh: 在 Tcl 中，因为一切都是字符串，所以你就是解释器。

blocks.html_en: For instance, if you aren't careful with grouping or don't understand the differences between the grouping types (braces {} vs. quotes ""), you can end up with double substitutions that lead to security vulnerabilities or bugs that are hard to trace in a large tool.

sentences.en: For instance, if you aren't careful with grouping or don't understand the differences between the grouping types (braces {} vs. quotes ""), you can end up with double substitutions that lead to security vulnerabilities or bugs that are hard to trace in a large tool.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果您在分组时不小心或者不了解分组类型之间的差异（大括号 {} 与引号“”），则最终可能会出现双重替换，从而导致在大型工具中难以追踪的安全漏洞或错误。

blocks.html_en: Trying to do deeply nested command calls within other command calls will quickly make the code unreadable. This should make programmers realize that breaking code into smaller blocks and opting for a line-by-line and step-by-step execution is a better approach. But it doesn't guarantee that all devs would do this, because Tcl doesn't impose any particular coding style and restrictions on you, like Python does for example.

sentences.en: Trying to do deeply nested command calls within other command calls will quickly make the code unreadable.
sentences.zh: 尝试在其他命令调用中进行深度嵌套的命令调用很快就会使代码变得不可读。

sentences.en: This should make programmers realize that breaking code into smaller blocks and opting for a line-by-line and step-by-step execution is a better approach.
sentences.zh: 这应该让程序员意识到，将代码分解成更小的块并选择逐行、逐步执行是更好的方法。

sentences.en: But it doesn't guarantee that all devs would do this, because Tcl doesn't impose any particular coding style and restrictions on you, like Python does for example.
sentences.zh: 但它并不能保证所有开发人员都会这样做，因为 Tcl 不会像 Python 那样对您强加任何特定的编码风格和限制。

blocks.html_en: Because Tcl provides the tools to redefine the language itself, it incentivizes a level of "cleverness" that is rarely seen in more rigid environments. What begins as a small, elegant script can rapidly mutate into an unmaintainable maze of custom commands and fragile substitution chains, simply because the programmer wanted to "look cool". Without the guardrails of enforced style or strict typing, the "quirks" of the language can move from being minor annoyances to becoming structural liabilities. To understand why Tcl can feel like a minefield, one must look closely at the specific mechanical behaviors where this "simplicity" breaks down in practice, and needs self-imposed guardrails or "wrapper" commands.

sentences.en: Because Tcl provides the tools to redefine the language itself, it incentivizes a level of "cleverness" that is rarely seen in more rigid environments.
sentences.zh: 因为 Tcl 提供了重新定义语言本身的工具，所以它激发了一定程度的“聪明”，这在更严格的环境中很少见。

sentences.en: What begins as a small, elegant script can rapidly mutate into an unmaintainable maze of custom commands and fragile substitution chains, simply because the programmer wanted to "look cool".
sentences.zh: 一开始是一个小而优雅的脚本，可以迅速变异成一个难以维护的自定义命令迷宫和脆弱的替换链，仅仅是因为程序员想要“看起来很酷”。

sentences.en: Without the guardrails of enforced style or strict typing, the "quirks" of the language can move from being minor annoyances to becoming structural liabilities.

blocks.html_en: Note on Tk widgets: In Tcl/Tk, creating a widget like ttk::button .mybtn creates a command. Just like TclOO "objects", widgets do not die when the proc ends. If you create a popup window or a frame inside a procedure, it will live forever until you manually destroy the .path to the widget. Thankfully, you don't need to extend managed_create to support Tk widgets! — Destroying any Tk widget also destroys all of its child widgets. Therefore, whenever possible, avoid creating widgets directly on the root — .mybtn or .mylbl — and instead parent them under a container widget — frame or canvas, like so: ttk::button .myfrm.mybtn. Then, whenever you need to clean up a whole tree of widgets parented under that container, simply call destroy .myfrm.

blocks.html_en: No Centralized Package Manager

sentences.en: No Centralized Package Manager
sentences.zh: 没有集中的包管理器

blocks.html_en: Tcl lacks a modern, ubiquitous package manager like npm or pip. While teacup existed for ActiveTcl, it’s largely legacy. This means that you either have to go hunting for packages or extensions, to download them compiled, or as source code to compile yourself. Or simply rely on what's commonly called a Tcl/Tk "Batteries Included" Distribution. These are third-party binary distributions, which include all sorts of battle- and time-tested packages out of the box, and therefore allow a one-time installation to cover the vast majority of Tcl/Tk use-cases. In a way, this mirrors the C#/.NET experience where you install the SDK and "everything just works" out of the box, except without nuget to pull new packages for you on request.

blocks.html_en: • BAWT — configurable framework by Paul Obermeier that automates creating custom BI distributions. Certain precompiled installers are also available, primarily for Windows, It includes almost anything that can be compiled for Tcl 9, even if it hasn't been fully stress-tested. It’s a "maximalist's" Tcl/Tk distribution, aimed at seasoned developers who know precisely what they're doing and why they might need largely outdated packages like tix. But the true value of BAWT is in the fact that Mr. Obermeier provides all the tools necessary to build a functional, portable Tcl/Tk distribution for several platforms and CPU architectures. It's precisely how I was able to get Tcl/Tk 9.0.3 working on a small Arm-based SBC — by compiling Tcl/Tk and all the packages I wanted to include, directly for the Arm64 platform

blocks.html_en: • ActiveState — listed here just for posterity. This was once the undisputed king of Tcl distributions. Apparently, if you were a Tcl developer between 2000 and 2015, ActiveTcl was your default choice. But then at some point ActiveState realized that big banks and insurance companies have millions of lines of existing Tcl 8.4/8.5 code that they couldn't easily migrate from, and needed help in maintaining all of that infrastructure. This signaled a shift in ActiveState's business strategy, and led to the death of the legendary teapot package manager, which ActiveState maintained between years 2000 and ~2020. What this means for the rest of us is — ignore ActiveState. They're a ghost of the past, focused on their own business, and no longer of any value to a random developer who just wants a versatile Tcl/Tk BI package or an installer

blocks.html_en: Do You Need a Package Manager?

sentences.en: Do You Need a Package Manager?
sentences.zh: 您需要包管理器吗？

blocks.html_en: While the fact that Tcl lacks a centralized package manager may seem like a huge downside for a "modern" developer, it also arguably improves Tcl/Tk's embeddability and, in a way, — security.

sentences.en: While the fact that Tcl lacks a centralized package manager may seem like a huge downside for a "modern" developer, it also arguably improves Tcl/Tk's embeddability and, in a way, — security.
sentences.zh: 虽然 Tcl 缺乏集中式包管理器这一事实对于“现代”开发人员来说似乎是一个巨大的缺点，但它也可以说提高了 Tcl/Tk 的嵌入性，并在某种程度上提高了安全性。

blocks.html_en: A Tcl/Tk "Batteries Included" distribution can be as small as just 35MB in case of Magicsplat (or a BAWT build with a similar composition). One such installer contains the most significant achievements of over 38 years of the Tcl/Tk development ecosystem. The vast majority of the packages you'll find in a BI distribution have been heavily time- and battle-tested, so you can confidently use them for mission-critical tasks. This, as you can imagine, also largely trivializes the deployment of Tcl/Tk on systems: with just 1 installer you can replicate your entire dev environment and be sure that every single script will function precisely as expected.

blocks.html_en: I can't stress enough, just how much Tcl/Tk has changed my approach to "compute management", as I've simply deployed it to all of my machines and gained a super-power to run the same GUI Tk script on any of my machines, without the need to recompile for each or having to develop strictly on the target platform itself. It's something you cannot do with any of the existing interpreted languages. Python could be an exception, since Tk GUI code can be embedded into Python scripts and run with tkinter, but it comes with a barebones, outdated version of Tcl and lacks most of the essential, powerful Tcl packages. Packages which come standard with a BI Tcl/Tk distribution: 100% ready to use and natively compiled for a platform you deploy Tcl/Tk to.

blocks.html_en: As for security, I could try and leverage the fact that you have to manually look for packages and often even compile them yourself, which makes it harder for you to become a victim of a supply chain attack. I could also mention that with Python all you need to do is pip install --upgrade some-package to download an updated, potentially compromised code bundle to your machine, including all of the tens of dependencies it also needs you to have updated, and the risks that arise from that.

blocks.html_en: Arguing that "Tcl/Tk is more secure because it has no package manager" would be dishonest. Do I personally know Mr. Nadkarni, or Mr. Obermeier? No. But I do know that both of them are key figures in the Tcl dev circles, and to nefariously compromise a package or two would do tremendous damage to their credibility. So I'd rather trust one of these guys, than a hundred random devs on the internet, who at some point might decide to suddenly mix their political views into their codebases, and cause damage — something I previously covered on the blog: The "node-ipc" Node.js package controversy.

blocks.html_en: In contrast, this is the area where C-like or strictly-typed languages shine simply due to their "syntactic rigidity". When it comes to the homoiconic Tcl, code can be both logic and data at any time, and code-generation is at the core of the language. Such flexibility, naturally, comes at a cost of the machine having difficulties with static code analysis. Doesn't mean there are no good code checkers/analyzers — Nagelfar is one of the more sophisticated linters available for this purpose, but it relies on syntax tables. So it sees a string, not a function call. It cannot verify arguments for a command it doesn't know exists yet, for instance, or determine if a dynamically modified command is valid until runtime.

blocks.html_en: As a result of the "Everything Is a String" paradigm, Tcl isn't ideal for working with specialized data types like vectors or matrices. To be clear, these, too, can be represented as strings, but the issue is the efficiency. While you can represent a 1GB matrix as a string or a list, you shouldn't because of the memory and CPU overhead of Tcl internal object management. And although a VecTcl package is available for the language, you'll likely just waste time trying to do linear math in Tcl.

blocks.html_en: Tcl offers a trade-off: it gives up JIT-speed for a rock-solid, almost 40-year stable C API that makes "gluing" a C++ matrix engine to build CLI and cross-platform GUI apps quicker than in almost any other language. blocks.html_en: • "The Tcl 9 Programming Language A Comprehensive Guide" by Ashok P. Nadkarni. A brilliant book written by a brilliant engineer that covers pure Tcl (without Tk). It's sort of considered "overkill" for "casual" Tcl users because it covers a lot of advanced topics. Doesn't mean you should skip it! Quite the contrary, this should be your first book on Tcl 9.0. It's extremely precise with concepts and explanations. But, boy, does Mr. Nadkarni love to condense his explanations so much that they need to be unpacked 2- or even 3-fold! For instance, by the end, in the "Coroutines" section, I was really struggling with the examples given, and had to painstakingly go though them line by line, to understand what was happening, and most importantly — why. Simply running the examples in the tclsh console wasn't helping much, since the results would simply match those in the book. So I had to place debug messages everywhere to understand the flow. To me (admittedly not sharpest tool in the shed) a lot of those seemed "too clever" and if implemented in real programs could end up generating substantial maintenance debt simply due to many of them being purely "academic". Again, it really is one of the more sophisticated books on Tcl, and if you ever decide to seriously pick up the language, you'll have to go though the book at least twice, to get a better grasp of the full capabilities of Tcl 9. I highly recommend it

blocks.html_en: Here's the deal: macOS is a very "opinionated" OS. Which makes sense, since Apple holds a tight grip over it down to the minute detail. They also don't shy away from changing it drastically from version to version, often breaking backwards compatibility. For instance, Apple will phase out their Rosetta 2 emulator starting with macOS 28. Rosetta is what allowed Macs with Apple silicon to run apps that were built for Macs with an Intel processor (x86 architecture) by translating code on the fly. Therefore, you first need to decide which Tcl build you're after — Intel or M-series/ARM one. Most likely it's the latter, so let's move on.

blocks.html_en: Which not only means you absolutely need to replace it, you'll also have to fight this default installation, as the system paths point to this legacy bundle. And if it's already missing entirely in your latest version of macOS — you're in luck, and now only need to install the modern Tcl/Tk binaries.

blocks.html_en: • Homebrew — sort of a "standard" way to install the latest Tcl/Tk on Macs. It installs to /opt/homebrew and tries to integrate better into the OS. It is a simpler install, but can occasionally break when Apple makes major OS changes (allegedly)

blocks.html_en: • MacPorts — while Homebrew is the popular choice, MacPorts is technically a more "self-contained" option. It installs everything Tcl into /opt/local, doesn't try to use Apple’s system libraries, and instead brings its own versions of extensions (OpenSSL, SQLite, etc.). This makes it super stable but results in longer install times because it often compiles from source. MacPorts is apparently also famous for its dependency hell: if you want to install Tcl, it might decide to install 40 other packages first, and the resulting Tcl/Tk install will take much more disk space. Fun fact: MacPorts itself is largely written in Tcl

It installs everything Tcl into /opt/local, doesn't try to use Apple’s system libraries, and instead brings its own versions of extensions (OpenSSL, SQLite, etc.).

sentences.en: This makes it super stable but results in longer install times because it often compiles from source.
sentences.zh: 这使得它超级稳定，但会导致安装时间更长，因为它通常是从源代码编译的。

sentences.en: MacPorts is apparently also famous for its dependency hell: if you want to install Tcl, it might decide to install 40 other packages first, and the resulting Tcl/Tk install will take much more disk space.
sentences.zh: MacPorts 显然也因其依赖地狱而闻名：如果您想安装 Tcl，它可能会决定首先安装 40 个其他软件包，而最终的 Tcl/Tk 安装将占用更多的磁盘空间。

sentences.en: Fun fact: MacPorts itself is largely written in Tcl
sentences.zh: 有趣的事实：MacPorts 本身主要是用 Tcl 编写的

This is the most "experimental" option mostly for cases when everything else failed, no idea whether it works or not

blocks.html_en: Embrace boring technology.

blocks.html_en: To circle back to the beginning of this guide, my journey started with a simple search for a cross-platform UI framework. With Tcl/Tk I found so much more than that. I got my hands on a robust, time- and battle-tested, cross-platform and extremely versatile "manager's helper" tool-set. I also discovered a new world of programming languages, where code and data are interchangeable, which made me look differently at programming as a hobby and as a profession. It inspired me.

sentences.en: With Tcl/Tk I found so much more than that.
sentences.zh: 通过 Tcl/Tk，我发现的远不止这些。

sentences.en: I got my hands on a robust, time- and battle-tested, cross-platform and extremely versatile "manager's helper" tool-set.
sentences.zh: 我得到了一个强大的、经过时间和战斗考验的、跨平台的、用途极其广泛的“经理的帮手”工具集。

sentences.en: I also discovered a new world of programming languages, where code and data are interchangeable, which made me look differently at programming as a hobby and as a profession.
sentences.zh: 我还发现了编程语言的新世界，其中代码和数据是可以互换的，这让我对编程作为一种爱好和一种职业有了不同的看法。

sentences.en: It inspired me.
sentences.zh: 这启发了我。

blocks.html_en: Learning Tcl/Tk and developing tools with it felt almost surreal. Like going back to the times of good old reliable technology, one that doesn't change simply because some project manager, or a tech lead, had decided their stack needed more "bling", or that it had to suddenly catch up to the younger, more agile, yet much less tested tools and concepts, breaking backwards-compatibility and causing panic attacks for their developer- and user-bases.

sentences.en: Learning Tcl/Tk and developing tools with it felt almost surreal.
sentences.zh: 学习 Tcl/Tk 并用它开发工具感觉几乎是超现实的。

sentences.en: Like going back to the times of good old reliable technology, one that doesn't change simply because some project manager, or a tech lead, had decided their stack needed more "bling", or that it had to suddenly catch up to the younger, more agile, yet much less tested tools and concepts, breaking backwards-compatibility and causing panic attacks for their developer- and user-bases.
sentences.zh: 就像回到古老可靠技术的时代一样，这种技术不会仅仅因为某些项目经理或技术主管决定他们的堆栈需要更多“闪亮”而改变，或者它必须突然赶上更年轻、更敏捷、但测试较少的工具和概念，破坏向后兼容性并引起开发人员和用户群的恐慌。

blocks.html_en: I have to be honest though: Tcl lacks any meaningful community apart from the team of its core maintainers. So using it may make you feel "lonely", simply because it's not a trendy language. It's a language of small teams, or professionals using it to build pragmatic tools, or work with mission-critical systems "in the background". They value reliability and consistency over the dynamically-changing ecosystems like Python, Node.js, JavaScript or TypeScript. They sleep well, knowing that in a week, in a year, or even in a decade, their code will run just as it did before. They focus on solving actual problems instead of fighting their own toolchain, and quietly maintain the systems that the rest of the world takes for granted.

sentences.en: They value reliability and consistency over the dynamically-changing ecosystems like Python, Node.js, JavaScript or TypeScript.

sentences.en: They sleep well, knowing that in a week, in a year, or even in a decade, their code will run just as it did before.
sentences.zh: 他们睡得很好，知道一周、一年甚至十年后，他们的代码将像以前一样运行。

sentences.en: They focus on solving actual problems instead of fighting their own toolchain, and quietly maintain the systems that the rest of the world takes for granted.

content_html_zh:
如果我告诉你存在一种语言或整个工具包：

  • 可用于创建跨平台控制台和 GUI 工具或应用程序
  • Those GUI apps look native on Windows, Linux and macOS
  • 支持安全高效的线程、非阻塞事件和 I/O
  • 安装了最常见的软件包后，占用空间约为 100MB
  • 可以为任何支持的平台生成非常紧凑的单文件应用程序
  • 能够构建强大的跨平台 Web 应用程序
  • 已存在并被一些最大的公司使用了三十多年
  • 免费且获得 BSD 许可，因此您可以用它做任何您想做的事情

你相信我吗？

前言

我所做的就是记录有关有趣或有用主题的个人经历。 实时可视化、3D 模拟、数据安全、能源效率，甚至输入设备、微控制器和健身——新研究和探索的源源不断的想法总是在待办事项列表中。

这个特定的主题比我最初计划的要复杂得多。 但我保证：这里的所有信息都是我自己在开始 Tcl/Tk 工具包学习之旅之前希望了解的信息。

我在与 Tcl/Tk 的蜜月期结束很久之后才写下这篇文章，并且会尽力做到客观和诚实。 既对你，也对我自己。 除了我的个人经验之外，我没有什么可以“推销”的，如果您决定尝试一下 Tcl/Tk，希望能够更好地为您提供信息并简化“入职”流程。

由于其以命令为中心的性质，Tcl 是一种功能强大但被广泛误解的语言。 我想为这次对话做出贡献，旨在通过简洁的解释和具体的例子来消除这种持续存在的困惑。 当然，还有一点天赋，让您开心。

请注意：我们在这里跳过“编程 101”演讲，假设您已经对通用编程逻辑有基本的了解。 如果您熟悉 if 语句并知道什么是函数，那么您可能已经准备好直接深入了解 Tcl 特定的结构和语法。 将本文视为“Tcl 入门和入门”，希望能让您也发现并欣赏这项近 40 年前悄然为世界提供动力的技术。 也许还能说服你亲自尝试一下，并传播出去。

至于“关于作者”——如果您有兴趣，请访问“关于”页面。

准备好？ 我们走吧。

介绍

有大量的变革性发明最终造福了整个人类：印刷机、电力或晶体管。 至于知识共享，当然有 Linux 操作系统、万维网协议和公钥密码学的概念。 你知道，我们通常认为理所当然的东西，或者甚至不知道的东西存在。

Tcl，即“工具命令语言”，由 John Ousterhout 于 1990 年创建并发布，在人类思维最伟大的产品中占有一席之地。 尤其是与更知名的图形用户界面工具包 — Tk 结合使用时。 1997 年，Ousterhout 荣获 Tcl/Tk 的 ACM 软件系统奖，该奖项颁发给因开发具有持久影响力的软件系统而受到认可的机构或个人，这种影响体现在对概念的贡献、商业接受度或两者兼而有之。

可以在项目的源代码存储库中找到有关 Tcl 的全面概述：

Tcl 提供了一个强大的平台，用于创建将不同应用程序、协议、设备和框架结合在一起的集成应用程序。 与 Tk 工具包配合使用时，Tcl 提供了最快、最强大的方式来创建在 PC、Unix 和 macOS 上运行的 GUI 应用程序。 Tcl 还可用于各种与 Web 相关的任务以及为应用程序创建强大的命令语言。 Tcl 由 Tcl 社区免费维护、增强和分发。 源代码开发以及错误报告和功能请求的跟踪在 core.tcl-lang.org 上进行。 Tcl/Tk 发布和邮件列表服务由 SourceForge 托管，Tcl Developer Xchange 托管在 www.tcl-lang.org。 Tcl 是一个免费提供的开源软件包。 您几乎可以用它做任何您喜欢的事情，例如修改它、重新分发它以及全部或部分出售它。 有关完整信息，请参阅文件“license.terms”。

好吧，好吧…… 但这一切意味着什么，您为什么要关心呢？

为什么

前段时间，我需要开发一个具有图形用户界面的跨平台桌面应用程序，该应用程序可以在 Windows 和 Linux (X11/Wayland) 上运行。 在此之前，我花了数年时间使用 AutoHotkey 来构建小型 Windows 实用程序，就像我在 Alt ♫ Code ♥ Numpad Emulation 上的文章中提到的那样。

AutoHotkey，特别是v2，实际上非常有能力，并且适合开发小型GUI工具，而不仅仅是做“热键相关的东西”。 凭借改进的“类 C”语法，对于具有广泛 JavaScript、PHP 或 C# 背景的人来说，使用起来会很愉快。

唯一的问题是什么？ — 仅适用于 Windows。 当然，借助 Wine 兼容层，AHK 脚本和单文件可执行文件可以在 Linux 中运行，但不能保证 AutoHotkey 所依赖的所有 Windows 特定绑定和本机库调用都能正常工作，或者根本无法工作。

我研究了其他选项来追求跨平台 GUI 框架和/或运行时：

  • C# 与 WinForms — 我首先考虑了 .NET 生态系统，但 WinForms 从根本上仍然与 Windows API 相关。 即使具有现代 .NET 跨平台功能，在 Linux 或 macOS 上实现真正的本机外观和感觉也需要迁移到 MAUI 或 Avalonia，这两者都带有巨大的依赖足迹，并且使用它来开发“非企业”软件非常痛苦。
  • 无头本地 Web 服务器（“类似电子”的方法）——我探索了在现代解耦架构中构建一个工具。 一个无头后端，设置本地 HTTP API 并提供基于浏览器的前端。 虽然这实现了与任何操作系统几乎 100% 的兼容性，并且或多或少被认为是现代应用程序的“事实上的标准”，但这种复杂性对于一个小工具来说是巨大的杀伤力。 您需要管理前端/后端通信、端口冲突和安全开销，只是为了在浏览器选项卡中呈现一个按钮，而该选项卡仅呈现一个空页面就消耗超过 100MB 的空间。 这并不是说我不想创建这样的应用程序。 我只是不希望我的选择仅限于这种类型的界面，这在很大程度上取决于所提供的浏览器的功能完整性
  • Go (Golang) 与 Fyne/Gio — 虽然 Go 生成高效的二进制文件，但开发人员对其可用的 UI 库的体验很快就陷入了“依赖地狱”。 创建一个简单的“Hello World”窗口引入了 40,000 个间接依赖项！ 生成的静态二进制文件超过 30MB，看起来一点也不像“原生应用程序”
  • Qt（通过 C++ 或 Python）——当然，我研究了 Qt，“行业标准”。 可惜的是，其元对象编译器 (MOC) 的复杂性、跨本机边界的信号和槽的混乱以及令人困惑的许可模型（GPL/LGPL 与商业）也使其成为一种禁忌。

这时我意识到 GUI 应用程序的现代“跨平台”解决方案实际上并不是通过可移植性实现跨平台的。 相反，它们只是打包环境，将所有垃圾带到需要运行的任何地方，简单地编译为在目标操作系统/CPU 组合上执行。 它们不会利用操作系统的本机 UI API 调用，而是“在画布上绘制像素”，这就是为什么此类 GUI 很少看起来像本机应用程序。

必须有更好的方法来开发跨平台应用程序和工具！

就在那时，我偶然发现了一些“Tk 工具包”的提及，并决定研究它，最终陷入了一个充满惊人发现的兔子洞……

认识 Tcl/Tk

在继续阅读之前，请花 40 分钟观看 Tcl 概述视频。 它将让您快速了解 Tcl 的历史和当前状态，同时让我避免将所有内容都倾销到这篇已经很庞大的帖子中。 不要费太多力气去理解视频中的所有代码示例，只要大致了解 Tcl 何时、为何以及如何出现就足够了。

长话短说，Tcl 是一种多功能的“架构粘合剂”，将高性能编译代码与灵活的、人类可读的逻辑层粘合在一起。

在软件中，“粘合语言”是一种编程语言，用于连接、管理和自动化单独的、预先存在的软件组件，这些组件最初并不是为了协同工作而设计的。 “粘合”不是从头开始构建核心逻辑，而是用于： 桥接：将高级用户界面连接到低级高性能代码（如 C++ 或 Rust） 编排：控制不同程序或模块之间的数据流 包装：提供简单的可编写脚本的命令来触发复杂的底层流程 “粘合”代码不执行繁重的计算，而是协调执行繁重计算的组件。

起初，Tcl 纯粹是作为一种编程语言实现的，具有自己的高级解释器，但 Ousterhout 先生很快意识到命令行应用程序在用户交互方面有其局限性，因此使用 Tk（一种跨平台图形用户界面工具包）对该语言进行了扩展。 这就是为什么每当提到该语言时，您经常会看到使用“Tcl/Tk”名称，因为 Tk 变得非常流行，这也是首先使用 Tcl 的关键原因之一。

由于 Tk 是 Tcl 的核心部分，因此要将控制台应用程序转变为 GUI 应用程序，您所需要做的就是“请求”Tk 包。 将要！ 现在，您只需少量代码即可构建具有本机外观的图形用户界面。

是的，就是这么简单，看一下：

将 Tk 与 Tcl 的关系视为 Unity 引擎/虚幻引擎与 OpenGL/Vulkan 的关系。 大多数游戏开发人员将“我是 Unity 开发人员”放入他们的 BIO 中，而不是“我是 OpenGL 开发人员”。 抽象层（或者 Tcl 中的 Tk 扩展）是价值和社区所在的地方，而底层语言则成为专门的“实现细节”。 作为视觉效果程序员，您当然至少应该了解低级 OpenGL 或 Vulcan API 的基础知识，但很可能 80% 的代码将与您使用的游戏引擎提供的高级抽象 API 进行交互。

Tcl is also a semantically simple language, with a very well-written C-implementation. Which is why it's available for most platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS, and Android with Termux for CLI Tcl apps, or Androwish (Android) and iWish (iOS) mobile apps to run GUI scripts, with a variety of CPU architectures supported — ARM, x86, RISC-V etc.

没有什么能让纯粹的 Tcl 特别…… 与其他语言相比，作为一种解释语言很特殊。 尽管有一些功能使 Tcl 脱颖而出：事件驱动的理念、同像性、“一切都是字符串”方法（我们将在本文中讨论这些功能），但它们并不是编写功能软件的唯一方法。 实际上，与 JavaScript、Python 甚至 Lua 和 Perl 等更“僵化/结构化”的语言相比，Tcl 的极端灵活性（代码就是数据，数据就是代码）使得现代开发人员更难掌握。

那么，Tcl过去和现在的闪光点在哪里呢？

《英雄不披斗篷》

别担心，我来这里并不是要告诉您“编程世界不公平地忘记了 Tcl，而它却是有史以来最好的东西！”

你看。 TCL只是…… 那里。

这是最讽刺的一点。 虽然它是最不“流行”的语言之一，但近 40 年来它一直并且仍然被广泛使用：为关键任务系统、高端网络硬件或协调最大银行的交易提供支持。 因为Tcl是如此之小（核心只是C），所以它被嵌入到我们每天使用的东西中而不自知：

  • Git：每个 Git 安装附带的 git gui 和 gitk 工具都是 Tcl/Tk 应用程序。 它们看起来“旧”，因为它们仍然使用经典的 Tk 小部件，但它们几乎“坚不可摧”，并且可以在每个操作系统上运行而无需依赖
  • FPGA/芯片：几乎所有主要硬件设计工具（Xilinx、Altera、Cadence）都使用 Tcl 作为其主要自动化语言
  • 网络设备：Cisco IOS 在路由器中内置了一个 Tcl 解释器，用于“嵌入式事件管理器”脚本
  • Intel、NVIDIA 和 AMD：这些公司的工程师使用 Tcl/Tk 构建控制大规模模拟场和硬件测试仪的内部 GUI
  • 西门子 EDA（以前称为 Mentor Graphics）：他们价值数百万美元的软件套件（如 Calibre 或 Virtuoso）使用 Tcl 作为用户编写与 GUI 和底层硬件模型交互的脚本的主要方式
  • ESA：欧洲航天局及其相关航空航天合作伙伴是 Tcl/Tk 的大量用户。 欧洲主要航空航天实验室（例如荷兰的 ESTEC 或德国的 ESOC）都在其最关键操作的后台运行 Tcl/Tk 应用程序

Tcl 随处可见，其中可靠性、向后兼容性和跨平台兼容性是第一位的。

惊讶吗？ 我确实是。 使用 Tcl/Tk，您可以编写 CLI 和 GUI 工具，这些工具可以在从核电站终端到 Raspberry Pi 的所有设备上可靠运行，而无需重新编译任何内容。 您难道不想免费、无附加条件地获得如此强大的东西吗？

SQLite 连接

我应该提到，Tcl 和 SQLite 是由同一群聪明人设计的，其中包括 SQLite（世界上部署和使用最多的数据库引擎）的作者 Richard Hipp。

事实上，SQLite 首先是作为 Tcl 扩展创建的！ 这是 Hipp 本人的演讲，他解释了 SQLite 是如何诞生的，以及 SQLite 如此成功的最重要原因是它的“Tcl 过去”。 非常酷的谈话，我强烈推荐它。

在我们继续之前，关于 SQLite 和 Tcl 的一些很酷的事实：

  • 所有 SQLite 测试的一半是用 Tcl 编写的
  • 第三个版本，即 SQLite 的当前版本，在操作过程中使用双端口对象，类似于 Tcl（这个概念将在本文后面解释）
  • Tcl 被用作最终 SQLite 代码的“汇编器”，它接收超过 125 个输入源 C 文件，对它们进行一些严格的后处理，并生成超过 200K 行的最终源代码
